docs.title: Amie desktop app
docs.text:
Amie is a desktop workbench for small intent models. You write a Kotlin script in the sandbox, it trains a classifier on top of a BERT encoder, the result lands in the AMP/ folder next to the app, and from there you can read its metrics, draw them as charts in the console, serve the model over HTTP, and open package jars from the Amie server. Devices connected to the Amie backend have a dashboard (not reachable from the sidebar at the moment; see Devices).

This site is plain Markdown in the repository's docs/ folder, built with MkDocs (mkdocs.yml at the repository root). Read it on GitHub, or serve it:

mkdocs serve -a 127.0.0.1:8000      # live-reloading site at http://127.0.0.1:8000
mkdocs build                        # static site in build/docs-site/

docs.title: The app in one minute
docs.text:
1. Run ./gradlew :desktopApp:run. No account is needed: the app opens on the sandbox (signing in, under Account in Settings, only matters for publishing, backups and the package repository, see Signing in).
  2. In the sandbox, open the templates (the disk icon over the editor) and load one, or type a script, then press Run (⌘↵ / Ctrl+Enter). The dummy model is there from the start:
val m = initMod("dummy")                              // opens a session, or returns the open one
log(m.predict("turn the lights on"))                  // lights
log(m.inference("turn the lights on").first())        // lights:0.61
  1. Open Models (second sidebar icon), Sessions tab: the session is still open, with its log and a Terminate button. How sessions behave is in Running sessions. To train your own model:
val train = source("intents.csv")          // columns: text,label
val model = modelBuilder("intents", train)
metricsChart("intents")                    // F1 per label as bars
metricsHistory("intents")                  // accuracy and macro F1 over every build
  1. On the Models page every model is a component to configure, serve, open and publish, and every open session can be terminated there.

docs.title: The command line
docs.text:
amie [options] [script.kts [args] | -c code | command ...]

  -c code          runs the code
  -i               the prompt after the script, with its values defined
  -e, --env name   the env to run in
  --amp folder     the AMP folder, over AMIE_AMP_DIR and the default
  -v, --verbose    the internal lines too
  -q, --quiet      no banner at the prompt
  --version, -V    the version and the license line
  -h, --help       this; amie <command> --help for a command

docs.title: The commands
docs.text: Command Actions models list, build <csv> --name n [--test csv], validate <n>, serve <n> [--port], info <n> groups list, add <group> <models>, remove <group> [model], open <group> [texts]; --env for another env packages list, search [query], add <jar>, maven <coordinate>, test <jar>, info <jar>, config [jar] [key=value], setup <jar> envs list, new <name>, use <name>, show <name> templates list, show <name>, run <name>, export <name> --out <folder> sessions list, runs, terminate <name \| #id \| all> hf search <query> [--format] [--task] [--limit], info <repo>, import <repo> [--model-name] run run <file> [args] learn The book, Learn amie, offline in the browser; learn path prints where it is

docs.title: The script API in brief
docs.text:
Call What it does log, info, error, data A console line at that level; lists, maps and answers printed as such source, relate A labeled csv; a test file for it modelBuilder, buildOptions Trains and exports an intent model, with options fineTune, calibrate, versions, rollback Teaches a model more, makes its scores honest, the heads it had validateMetrics, confusionMatrix, mistakes, suspects The stored validation as tables initMod, sessionMod A session of a model, a package or an imported model; one for a block group The models of a group asked together packages The package jars: what the repositories offer, a download, a jar's check, metadata and tests; packages.config and packages.setConfig read and set its config files huggingFace, importModel A model of the Hub; one by its path. An encoder and decoder pair opens as .encoder and .decoder (pairs) serve, stopServing A model over HTTP ortClosable, ortStatic, ortRequired, ortLimited, ortAsync How long what a block opens lives database, shell, shellScript Postgres; the login shell implementation, environment A Maven package into the env; the env to run in coroutineTemplate, template, input, output A template in the background, and the two ends of its conversation handleBy, errorLog Running on after an error; what the text model makes of one

:api at the prompt has every function with its signature, and the Scripting API has the rest.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 The script finished, or the command did what it was asked 1 The script failed, or the command couldn't 2 A command line amie can't read

docs.title: Inside amie
docs.text:
amie is a Gradle module, amie, and reimplements nothing: the script engine, the model groups, the packages, the envs, the templates, the Hub imports and the model server live in the engine module it depends on, runtime, reached through one facade there, HeadlessAmie, the script runtime for a program with no window. No UI toolkit is on its class path.

The sources are short. Main.kt is the entry point and the exit codes, CommandLine.kt reads the command line, Repl.kt is the prompt, ScriptRun.kt runs a file as main.kts, and Commands.kt, ModelCommands.kt and Learn.kt are the commands. jdk.sh is the JDK 21 lookup, spliced into the built bin/amie and sourced by the launcher, and install.sh the install onto the PATH. The tests run against a folder of their own, never your AMP.

amie is free software: you can redistribute it and modify it under the GNU General Public License, version 3 or any later version. Its text is the LICENSE file at the root of the repository.

docs.title: The AMP folder
docs.text:
Everything the app writes lives in AMP/. Both ./gradlew :desktopApp:run and the packaged app (DMG, MSI, DEB) keep it in the user's application-data folder: ~/Library/Application Support/amie pilot/AMP on macOS, %APPDATA%\amie pilot\AMP on Windows, ~/.local/share/amie-pilot/AMP on Linux (under $XDG_DATA_HOME when that is set). The Gradle run task hands the app its resources folder, just as the packaged app has one, and that is what picks this folder. On its first start the folder is seeded from the AMP/ shipped inside the app (backend.json, keycloak.json, componentSettings.json, pluginDir/, env/, sample-intents.csv), which is made from amieApplication/desktopApp/AMP/ in the repository; the dummy model is written next. Started some other way, such as running MainKt straight from the IDE, the app keeps AMP/ in its working directory instead. AMIE_AMP_DIR names another folder in every case; the tests use it to work in amieApplication/desktopApp/build/test-amp. The amie.amp.dir system property does the same when AMIE_AMP_DIR isn't set: an exported bundle's runner uses it for the AMP/ beside it, and amie.models.dir for its models/bert/. Every model lives under models/, one folder per kind (below). Nothing is kept anywhere else on the machine, so copying this folder moves your scripts, models, metrics, plugins and sign-in to another checkout or machine.

Path What it holds Tracked in git pluginDir/main.kts The sandbox script, saved as you type yes pluginDir/assembly.kts The script as it was assembled for the last Run (the prelude, the env, main.kts) yes pluginDir/backup/main-<yyyyMMdd-HHmmss>.kts The script a template replaced in the editor; the Templates pane's Previous scripts. What a restore replaces is kept here too, named the same way after the file yes pluginDir/corePlugins.json The plugin jars importPlugin knows yes packages.json The plugins chosen per device on its configuration page yes <file>.csv A training or validation csv picked from elsewhere, copied in so the model can find it again yes .<name>-to-label.csv.next A queue being written; it replaces <name>-to-label.csv when complete no pluginDir/runs.jsonl The sandbox's last 20 runs, one line each: when it began (UTC), how long it took, whether it finished, a failed one's first error and what it used; Recent runs shows them. Not shipped in the packaged app no (this machine's runs) pluginDir/*.jar Package jars, opened by scripts with initMod("x.jar"); jars fetched from the Amie server land here yes pluginDir/*.jar.source.json Where a fetched jar came from: download URL, website page, version, fetch time; repo and sha for a jar from GitHub yes github.json The GitHub repositories package jars are looked for in (repos, default samging/jar-jar) and an optional token for private ones; written on first use no (it may hold a token) pluginDir/.incoming/ A downloaded jar while it is checked; removed when it fails the check no pluginDir/collections.json The package collections: name and member jars yes pluginDir/*.jar.package.json Metadata written beside a jar that ships none (or over the jar's own): config files, env, Java, entry class, tests yes pluginDir/*.jar.tests.json The last test run of that package: each test's input, answer, pass/fail yes pluginDir/config/<jar>/ The configuration files a package reads: its templates are written here, the package resolves them as resources yes env/<env>/groups.json The model groups of that env: name, models, icon yes env/<env>/<group>.sessions.log What the swarm of that group was asked and answered; when one of its models keeps no texts ("keepTexts": false), each text's length instead of the text, as in that model's own log and in the swarm's console lines. Its other models then log the texts the group asks them the same way, in their sessions.log and console lines; a text asked of one of them directly is logged as its own module.json says yes pluginDir/*.jar.sessions.log What every session of that package was asked and answered (open, run, error, close lines) yes models/intents/modules.json The registry of the models: each name and the folder under models/intents/ it lives in yes models/intents/<name>/model.onnx An exported model yes models/intents/<name>/dropped.csv The rows a build dropped, and why (only for a model that keeps texts) yes models/intents/<name>/icon.<ext> An uploaded icon (Upload image on the About tab) yes models/intents/<name>/module.json Its manifest: encoder, dimensions, labels; its version and what made it (kind: build, fine-tune, calibration, rollback; parentVersion, fineTunedOn), the rows per label it learned from (dataRows, fineTunedRows, for the model card), the temperature folded into its last layer, and the mean of its training features (featureMean, base64 floats, for a fine-tune without the data; not kept when keepTexts is false) yes models/intents/<name>/metrics.json One validation entry per build, fine-tune, calibration, validation or rollback (tables and charts read this) yes models/intents/<name>/guide.md The model's guide, its Guide tab, published with it; between its two amie:model-card marker lines the model card, written again after every run yes models/intents/<name>/versions/v<N>/ The ten heads before the current one: model.onnx, module.json and run.json (the run it was scored with), for rollback yes models/intents/<name>/serving.json Host, port, path, methods, listening, the min score and fallback label when set, and who may ask when set (apiKey, cors, maxBodyBytes, rateLimitPerMinute: Serving a model); an apiKey written $ENV:NAME is read from there when a request comes yes (with a key set it holds the key, so keep the tracked seed's keyless) models/intents/<name>/incoming.jsonl Requests the served model received yes models/intents/<name>/access.log (access.1.log) One line per request its listener answered, whatever the status (time, request id, client, method, path without query, status, ms, text length, bytes, outcome; never a text), and its start and stop lines; moved to access.1.log past 2 MB (Serving a model) yes templates/<id>.kts, templates/<id>.json The sandbox's script templates: the code, and its name, about, tags, source, env, lines, what it opens, times and loads; .seeded marks the first seeding done yes models/intents/<name>/plots/*.png The metrics plots (per run: scores, confusion, and for runs that kept them how the heads learned and the calibration; across runs; from the sessions), drawn again when metrics.json changes or when an older version of the app drew them (plots/.style says which style did); compare.png is the last comparison of a kept head with the current one (Compare under Versions), drawn by each comparison yes models/intents/<name>/sessions.log What every session of that model was asked and answered (open, run, error, close lines); for a model with "keepTexts": false in its module.json (built with buildOptions(keepTexts = false), like the model site's) each text's length instead of the text yes env/<name>/env.lock.json What a script environment has imported yes env/caches/ Maven downloads yes sample-intents.csv 45 text,label rows over greeting / lights / weather, written on first start for trying New model and Validate yes <name>-to-label.csv The model's queue: the texts it is least sure about (textsToLabel), the answers corrected on the Try line, and the unsure answers of a batch pasted there (queueGuesses), with its guess beside the label column. Renamed with the model, deleted when the model is destroyed no cache/embeddings/<encoder>-<hash>/vectors.bin, encoder.txt The sentence vector of every text embedded so far, keyed by the SHA-256 of the text (not the text), one store per encoder (encoder.txt names it); started again past 512 MB; nothing a model that keeps no texts embeds goes in (its builds, fine-tunes, calibrations and comparisons); embeddingCache.clear() empties it no relations.json Which test file belongs to which training file (relate) yes componentSettings.json Configured devices yes databases.json The Postgres connections a script opens with database("name"): url, user, password (any of them written $ENV:NAME reads an environment variable, or that line of a bundle's secrets.env), written with a main entry on first use no backend.json Amie backend, website and S3 service addresses yes keycloak.json Keycloak server, realm, client id and secret no session.json The signed-in session (access, refresh and id tokens) no settings.json The UI scale, where the sandbox's tool windows stand and how big they are, whether the Models page's sidebar shows, whether the first steps over the Models tab were dismissed (firstStepsHidden), the editor's text size (editorFontSize) and re-indent on Enter (reindentOnEnter) and Run details (runDetails); written at the first change yes logs.txt Everything the console showed, every level; past 20 MB it moves to logs.1.txt (replacing the one before), so two files are kept yes

docs.title: The models folder
docs.text:
Folder Holds Was, before November 2026 models/bert/, models/bert/bge/ The NER model and the bge encoder every intent model is trained on; ./scripts/setup.sh puts them there the same models/intents/<name>/ The trained intent models (the table above), with models/intents/modules.json as their registry modules/ models/text/<name>/ The text models, Llama and Qwen: ONNX Runtime GenAI exports textModels/ models/speech/<name>/ Whisper and the voices speech.jar runs pluginDir/config/speech/models/ models/imported/<name>/ Models brought in from outside, such as a Hugging Face repo: the downloaded files under their repo paths (onnx/model.onnx stays as it is) and a source.json; initMod("<name>") opens one new

The app moves an older folder into place when it starts (ModelsMigration, before anything reads a model): an old folder whose new one isn't there yet is renamed, on the same volume, so nothing is copied; a symbolic link moves as a link. When both are there nothing moves: the app reads the new one and the console says which folder to tidy. Nothing is deleted or overwritten, and every move is logged. A folder that can't be written is read as it is. speech.jar reads its models where models= in pluginDir/config/speech/speech.properties says, so the move sets that to models/speech when the setting is empty or names a folder that is gone; a setting that names a folder that is there is left alone. ModelFolders is the one owner of these paths in the code; until the next release it still reads an old folder whose new one isn't there.

An imported model's source.json says where it came from and which format to open it in:

{"source": "huggingface", "repo": "owner/name", "revision": "<commit sha>", "format": "onnx", "files": [{"path": "onnx/model.onnx", "size": 90387630}], "downloadedAt": "2026-11-06T10:00:00Z", "task": "text-classification", "labels": ["greeting", "lights", "weather"]}

format is onnx, torchscript, tensorflow or tflite; task is the Hub's pipeline tag (null when it has none) and labels what the model's config.json names (id2label, in order), both read by the Models page without opening the model; a source.json from before has neither, which reads as none. A download in progress lives in models/imported/.incoming/<name>/, each file as <path>.part until its size checks. The folder moves into place only when it is whole, so a folder under models/imported is always complete. A download cancelled from the Models page removes its .incoming folder; one cut short in any other way leaves it, for the next download to go on from.

docs.title: Configuration files
docs.text:
keycloak.json is written with defaults on first start:

{
  "baseUrl": "http://localhost:8080",
  "realm": "master",
  "clientId": "amie",
  "clientSecret": "<the amie client's secret>",
  "redirectPort": 48080
}

Environment variables KEYCLOAK_URL, KEYCLOAK_REALM, KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_ID, KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_SECRET override it.

backend.json names the Amie backend, the website and the S3 service that keeps package jars; AMIE_BACKEND_URL, AMIE_SITE_URL and AMIE_S3_URL override it. With Keycloak on port 8080, run the backend on another port (AMIE_BACKEND_PORT=8090) and set baseUrl here.

docs.title: Metrics format
docs.text:
metrics.json is a list of runs; the last one is the current model:

{
  "runs": [
    {
      "createdAt": "2026-10-14T14:02:11Z",
      "samples": 240, "trainSize": 192, "validationSize": 48,
      "accuracy": 0.917, "macroF1": 0.905,
      "labels": { "lights": { "precision": 0.933, "recall": 0.933, "f1": 0.933, "support": 15 } },
      "confusion": [[14, 1], [1, 14]],
      "warnings": [],
      "validation": "split 20%"
    }
  ]
}

confusion[truth][prediction] is indexed like the label list in module.json.

Times in these files (createdAt here, in module.json and in groups.json, a package report's ranAt, a jar's fetchedAt) are instants in UTC, as the trailing Z says; the Models page and the console show them in this machine's local time. A time written into text that is kept, such as a rollback's note ("v1 brought back (made 2026-10-21 04:03 +02:00), replacing v2"), carries its offset from UTC, so it reads right on any machine.

Runs written since versions are kept carry more, all optional (older runs have none of it and read the same): kind (build, fine-tune, calibration, validation, rollback) and version; analysis with ece, the reliability bins, the selective gates, the mistakes and suspects (texts only when the model keeps texts), the temperature, eceBefore and a fine-tune's learning curve; baseline, the head before a fine-tune or a calibration scored on the same rows; accuracyRange and macroF1Range (low, high: where the score fell in the middle 95% of 1,000 resamples of the run's rows, see how far the scores hold); leakage (checked, exact, near, the warning it gave, and for a model that keeps texts up to ten pairs of a scored row and the row it learned from, see rows it learned from); and a note. Each entry of candidates adds the cross-validation scores (cvAccuracy, cvMacroF1, cvSpread, folds), where early stopping stopped and which epoch it kept (stoppedAt, keptEpoch), and its learning curve (up to 41 points of loss and accuracy on the training and validation rows).

docs.title: How the app works today
docs.text: Four pictures of what the code does on 2026-11-03: how the app starts, what a Run does, how initMod(name) becomes a session, and the talk loop of voice/talk-to-amie.kts. Every box is a file; the table under each diagram links it. Paths are under amieApplication/desktopApp/src/main/kotlin/org/example/project/ unless written in full. The diagrams were checked against a real run (the console's logs.txt), not against a plan.

docs.title: 1. Start
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    main["main.kt<br/>main(args)"] --> flags{"--export or --bench?"}
    flags -- yes --> cmd["ExportCommand / BenchCommand<br/>runs and exits"]
    flags -- no --> oom["installOutOfMemoryHandler"] --> move["ModelsMigration.runOnce()<br/>modules/, textModels/ and the speech models<br/>renamed into AMP/models/, once"] --> app["application { Window }<br/>undecorated, 85% of the screen"]
    app --> chrome["AppChrome, FocusVisibility,<br/>UI scale from AppSettings"] --> base["AppBaseTemplate<br/>AmieTheme { Pages() }"]
    base --> nav["NavHost: start"] --> sandbox["codingSandbox<br/>WindowHeader + CodingSandbox(SandboxPanes.kept)"]
    nav -. "from the sidebar" .-> models["models: ModelsPage"]
    nav -. "from the sidebar" .-> settings["settings: SettingsPage"]

    subgraph background ["In the background, as the window shows"]
        direction TB
        backend["BackendConfig.resolve()<br/>fixes a backend.json on Keycloak's port"]
        restore["ModelServer.restore()<br/>models that were listening listen again<br/>(reads models/intents/*/serving.json)"]
        prewarm["after 4 s: ScriptEngineCache.prewarm()<br/>loads the Kotlin compiler on a low-priority thread"]
        runs["SandboxRuns.read()<br/>pluginDir/runs.jsonl → Recent runs"]
        autorun["AMIE_AUTORUN=1: the saved main.kts runs once"]
    end
    app -.-> backend
    base -.-> restore
    app -.-> prewarm
    sandbox -.-> runs
    sandbox -.-> autorun
    models -.-> poll["readSnapshot every 1.5 s<br/>modules, sessions, packages, groups"]
Box File What it does main(args) main.kt Hands --export and --bench to their commands, installs the out-of-memory handler, opens the window ModelsMigration.runOnce() amp/ModelsMigration.kt, amp/ModelFolders.kt Moves each kind of model into AMP/models/ with one atomic rename when its old folder is there and the new one is not; with both there it moves nothing and says which to tidy; it points speech.properties at models/speech. ModelFolders is the one owner of the paths every reader uses ExportCommand, BenchCommand export/ExportCommand.kt, bench/BenchCommand.kt The command-line modes; no window application { Window } main.kt The undecorated window, its tray icon when closed while a script runs, the resize edges AppChrome, FocusVisibility components/ui/viewport/AppChrome.kt, FocusRing.kt What every page's header gets from the window (drag, minimize, maximize, close) and the keyboard focus ring AppBaseTemplate components/render/templates/AppBaseTemplate.kt The theme and the NavHost: start goes straight to codingSandbox; models, settings, login and the device routes are the rest CodingSandbox sandbox/CodingSandbox.kt The sandbox page: editor, console, the tool windows; SandboxPanes.kept holds the run that outlives the page ModelsPage models/ModelsPage.kt The Models page, which reads readSnapshot every 1.5 s or slower when a read is slow (pollDelay) BackendConfig.resolve() backend/BackendConfig.kt Corrects AMP/backend.json before any backend call; nothing is called at start ModelServer.restore() runtime/ModelServer.kt Starts the listener of every model whose serving.json says it was listening ScriptEngineCache.prewarm() script/ScriptRuntime.kt After PREWARM_DELAY_MS (4 s) loads the Kotlin compiler so the first Run answers in a moment; off with -Damie.prewarm=false SandboxRuns.read() sandbox/SandboxRuns.kt The last 20 runs for the Recent runs list AMIE_AUTORUN sandbox/CodingSandbox.kt With AMIE_AUTORUN=1 the first sandbox shown presses Run once readSnapshot models/ModelsSnapshot.kt One read of everything the Models page shows

What a start marks on standard output with -Damie.timing=true: main entered, window content composed, sandbox composed, sandbox drawn, models page read (StartupTiming.kt).

docs.title: 2. A run
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    run["Run button or ⌘↵<br/>CodingSandbox"] --> start["MainScriptRun.start(code)<br/>clears the console, starts a RunMeter"]
    start --> plan["EnvPlan.scan(code)<br/>the env the script names and its imports"]
    plan --> env["ScriptEnvironments.open(env)<br/>env.source(plan): Maven and local jars → AMP/env/<env>/"]
    env --> loader["env.classLoader(...)<br/>the jars of the env over the app's classes"]
    loader --> engine["ScriptEngineCache.engineFor(loader)<br/>one Kotlin engine per class loader"]
    engine --> assemble["assembleScript(code)<br/>imports, val amie = bindings['logger'],<br/>the SandboxApi prelude, then the script"]
    assemble --> files["pluginDir/main.kts ← the code<br/>pluginDir/assembly.kts ← the assembled script"]
    files --> eval["engine.eval(assembly, bindings)<br/>on an IO thread, inside ScriptRuns.track"]
    eval --> logger["logger = SandboxLogger(env, gradleEngine, scope)<br/>the ScriptLogger the script calls"]
    logger --> console["logToConsole<br/>the console pane and AMP/logs.txt"]
    eval -- "template('x') / coroutineTemplate('x')" --> templates["TemplateRuns.start<br/>a saved template in an engine of its own,<br/>input() and output() over two channels"]
    eval -- "ends, fails or Stop" --> outcome["RunOutcome<br/>Resources line, pluginDir/runs.jsonl"]
    eval -- "stillOpenAtEnd" --> open["openSessionNames()<br/>what the run left open"]
Box File What it does Run sandbox/CodingSandbox.kt The button and the shortcut both call MainScriptRun.start MainScriptRun script/MainScriptRun.kt The one run of main.kts; it belongs to the app, so leaving the page does not end it EnvPlan, ScriptEnvironments, ScriptEnvironment envBuilder/ScriptEnvironment.kt The env named by settings { env = … } or the default; its env.lock.json, Maven resolution, the class loader ScriptEngineCache script/ScriptRuntime.kt One engine per class loader, the Gradle settings engine, prewarm assembleScript script/ScriptRuntime.kt What the engine really evaluates; ScriptErrors maps its line numbers back to main.kts SandboxApi.prelude() script/SandboxApi.kt One delegate line per API entry, so a script writes initMod(...) and not amie.initMod(...) SandboxLogger script/SandboxLogger.kt The ScriptLogger of a run: console lines, input(), the builders ScriptLogger script/ScriptLogger.kt The script API: initMod, sessionMod, group, modelBuilder, fineTune, serve, shell, the ort* blocks logToConsole console/ConsoleLog.kt Every console line, to the pane and to AMP/logs.txt TemplateRuns script/BackgroundTemplates.kt Background templates: template(name) ends with the run, coroutineTemplate(name) goes on ScriptRuns runtime/ScriptRuns.kt Tracks the run's thread: its cpu, allocation and the sessions it opened RunOutcome, SandboxRuns runtime/RunResources.kt, sandbox/SandboxRuns.kt The figures of the run and the record in pluginDir/runs.jsonl

The console says Running pluginDir/main.kts first, and the Resources line last, both at the internal level, off at start, so the console shows only what the script logs. A failure's lines begin with their place in main.kts.

docs.title: 3. initMod(name): a name becomes a session
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    call["initMod(name)<br/>ScriptLogger"] --> jar{"ends in .jar?"}
    jar -- yes --> open["JarPackages.open(name)<br/>env → AMP/pluginDir → a path → the server"]
    open --> meta["PackageMetadata.read, prepareConfig<br/>AMP/pluginDir/config/<jar>/ written from templates"]
    meta --> inst["URLClassLoader(config dir, jar)<br/>new instance, configure(dir)"]
    inst --> jsession["JarPackageSession<br/>run(text) = the class's run(String), close()"]
    jar -- no --> speech{"no module, no text model,<br/>but SpeechModels.has(name)?"}
    speech -- yes --> acquire["SpeechModels.acquire(name)<br/>whisper / voice as speech.properties names them"]
    acquire --> sjar["JarPackages.open('speech.jar')<br/>run('use <model>')"]
    sjar --> smodel["SpeechModel<br/>hear <wav> or say <text>"]
    speech -- no --> ms["ModelSessions.acquire(name)<br/>the open session of that name, else a new one"]

docs.title: 4. The talk: voice/talk-to-amie.kts
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    typed["Console: talk<br/>input() in main()"] --> block["ortClosable('talk to Amie')"]
    block --> opens["initMod: face.jar, microphone.jar, whisper, voice,<br/>mail.jar, browser.jar, mac.jar, spotify.jar, files.jar, memory.jar"]
    opens --> train{"hasModel('amie-intents')?"}
    train -- no --> build["modelBuilder('amie-intents', source('voice-actions.csv'))<br/>trains once → AMP/models/intents/amie-intents"]
    train -- yes --> intents["initMod('amie-intents')"]
    build --> intents
    intents --> llama["initMod('llama3.2-3b')<br/>'Loading the text model'"]
    llama --> access{"mic.run('access')"}
    access -- off --> sorry["speak: turn on the microphone<br/>return"]
    access -- on --> greet["speak('Good morning…')"]
    greet --> listen["listen(): face 'listen'<br/>mic.answer('listen turn') → wav or silence"]
    listen --> hear["hearing.answer(wav)<br/>speech.jar: hear → Whisper"]
    hear --> guess["intents.predictions(said)<br/>best label and score"]
    guess --> sure{"score ≥ 0.985?"}
    sure -- yes --> action["the label is the action"]
    sure -- no --> decide["decide(said, top 5 labels)<br/>Llama picks 'tool | details'"]
    decide --> action
    action --> careful{"brew_install, close_terminals, quit_app<br/>and not sure?"}
    careful -- yes --> ask["agreed(question): speak, listen"]
    careful -- no --> doit["when(action):<br/>a jar's run(...), a voice/*.sh script,<br/>or chat(said) through Llama"]
    ask --> doit
    doit --> speak["speak(text): face 'think'<br/>voice.answer(text) → speech.jar: say → Supertonic wav<br/>face 'talk', mic.run('play wav'), face 'smile'"]
    speak --> listen
    doit -- goodbye --> bye["speak('Talk soon!'), break<br/>the block closes every session"]

What logs.txt shows of one turn, in this order: Listening, the hear line of speech.jar, You: … -> action, the package's run line, Amie: …, the say line of speech.jar, the play line of microphone.jar.

docs.title: The code of amie: what is where, and why
docs.text: A reader's map of the amieCli repository: the two Kotlin modules, every package of the engine with what it is for and who uses it, how a process starts and runs a script, and the state it keeps. Written for learning the code, not for using amie; the amie guide covers the use.

docs.title: Size
docs.text:
Part Files Lines amie/src/main (the interpreter) 13 1 785 amie/src/test 5 428 runtime/src/main (the engine) 131 25 475 Gradle build files (*.kts) 7 679 Shell scripts (bin/amie, install.sh, jdk.sh, scripts/setup.sh, the voice scripts) 9 225 docs/*.md 23 5 831 The learn book, amie/learn/index.html 1 567 voice/ (scripts and data for the talk starter) 9 1 751

About 27 200 lines of Kotlin, of which the interpreter proper is about 6 %. Everything heavy is the engine, which is the script runtime of the amie pilot desktop app, taken out of it unchanged in November 2026.

docs.text:

  src/main/kotlin/org/amie/cli/
  src/test/kotlin/org/amie/cli/
  learn/index.html    the learn book, copied into the jar and opened by amie learn

The dependency runs one way: amie depends on runtime, runtime depends on nothing of amie. The desktop app, in its own repository, depends on the same runtime module.

docs.text:
File Lines What it holds Main.kt 70 Amie.main(args): parse, print help or version, else install the console, settle the AMP folder, dispatch CommandLine.kt 179 CommandLine.parse into an Invocation: Repl, Script, Code, Command, Help, Version, Usage; the usage text Output.kt 89 Where console lines go: stdout, errors on stderr, internal lines only with -v; the slf4j properties AmpFolder.kt 52 The AMP folder to work in: --amp, else AMIE_AMP_DIR, else the user's data folder; the DJL cache; the models migration ScriptRun.kt 63 A script as main.kts: read a file, a project or a starter, pass its arguments, run it, wait for the background, keep serving Repl.kt 268 The prompt: JLine line editing, ReplInput deciding when a block is complete, the colon commands, :help Commands.kt 315 The Command base class (actions, flags, help), Commands.all, and run, new, examples, sessions, envs, templates ModelCommands.kt 418 models (with info and remove for every kind), groups, packages, hf Picker.kt 114 The arrow-key list hf import picks files from: up and down, space takes or leaves, Enter, n leaves; redrawn in place, wrapped to the terminal Starters.kt 49 The starter scripts, from the engine's SandboxExamples, seeded into AMP/templates on first use Learn.kt 69 amie learn: the book copied to AMP/learn and opened in the browser Banner.kt 42 The banner and the version line Style.kt 57 ANSI colours for the prompt, errors, dimmed lines

docs.title: Desktop leftovers, and why they are still here
docs.text:
These came along with the split because something live imports them. None does useful work under amie.

Package Lines What it was for What still reaches it Could it go? auth 786 Keycloak sign-in for the app: password and browser flows, token checks, the session in AMP/session.json backend, settings, and C/export/BundleRunner.kt for a bundle's tokens. Under amie AuthState.user is always empty Yes, with the three callers made to compile without it backend 632 The app's web backend: saved state, package and module uploads, error reports, site and S3 addresses ConsoleLog calls ErrorReporter.report on every ERROR line (a no-op while nobody is signed in); ScriptLogger.saveState/loadState/listStates (fail without a token); JarPackages uses its HTTP client and BackendConfig addresses to fetch jars from the Amie server Mostly. Only the jar fetch does real work; BackendConfig and the client could stay as a smaller thing settings 700 The app's preferences and cloud sync of the AMP folder One read, AppSettings.current.value.assistantModel, when a script calls handleBy(); that read pulls in CloudSave, hence auth and backend Yes, with handleBy taking its model name from elsewhere data/remote/parser 23 Two DTOs of AMP/pluginDir/corePlugins.json SandboxLogger.importPlugin, which only prints the name Yes

The short answer to "why is the backend there": the engine logs every error through one function, and that function also offers the line to the app's error reporting, which needs the sign-in state, which needs the backend client. amie inherits the chain and never uses it, since no one signs in. Trimming it is a matter of giving those three call sites a smaller target, not of untangling the engine.

docs.title: Initialization: from the shell to a running script
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[bin/amie or ~/.local/bin/amie] --> B[jdk.sh: find a JDK 21, export JAVA_HOME]
    B --> C[MainKt.main → Amie.main]
    C --> D[CommandLine.parse → Invocation]
    D -->|help, version, usage| E[print, exit]
    D --> F[Output.install: slf4j levels, HeadlessAmie.useConsole]
    F --> G[AmpFolder.resolve: amie.amp.dir, DJL cache, ModelsMigration.runOnce]
    G --> H[HeadlessAmie.readInputFromStandardInput]
    H --> I{which invocation}
    I -->|Script, Code| J[ScriptRun.runCode]
    I -->|Repl| K[Repl.start]
    I -->|Command| L[Commands.find.run]
    J --> M[EnvPlan.withEnv when -e]
    M --> N[HeadlessAmie.run → ScriptRunner.run]
    N --> O[EnvPlan.scan: environment and implementation lines]
    O --> P[ScriptEnvironments.open.source: env.lock.json, Maven, jars, class loader]
    P --> Q[ScriptEngineCache.engineFor: the kts JSR-223 engine]
    Q --> R[assembleScript: imports, prelude, SettingsEnv, body → AMP/pluginDir/assembly.kts]
    R --> S[engine.eval under ScriptRuns.track]
    S --> T[awaitBackground, Serving.waitWhileListening]
    T --> U[HeadlessAmie.close: databases, jars, log file]

Step by step, with the file and function at each:

  1. The launcher. bin/amie sources amie/jdk.sh and rebuilds with ./gradlew :amie:installDist when a source is newer than the built binary, then execs amie/build/install/amie/bin/amie. The installed bin/amie is Gradle's start script with jdk.sh spliced in by tasks.startScripts in amie/build.gradle.kts. jdk.sh looks, in order, at AMIE_JAVA_HOME, JAVA_HOME, the Mac's java_home, Homebrew, ~/.local/lib/jdk-21, sdkman, /usr/lib/jvm and Gradle's downloaded JDKs, and exits with 2 when none is a 21. The JVM starts with -Damie.version, -Djava.awt.headless=true, -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=35 and the main class org.amie.cli.MainKt.
  2. Parsing. Main.kt: Amie.main calls CommandLine.parse. Options are -h, --version, -i, -v, -q, -e, --amp, -c; the first other word is looked up in Commands.all and becomes a Command, else a Script. Help, version and a usage mistake return here, before anything touches the disk.
  3. The console. Output.install sets the slf4j-simple levels (the engine's loggers to warn, DJL to error, the sandbox logger off) and calls HeadlessAmie.useConsole(::print), which sets headlessConsole in C/console/ConsoleLog.kt. From here every logToConsole line reaches Output.print: errors on stderr, internal lines only with -v, everything to AMP/logs.txt as well.
  4. The AMP folder. AmpFolder.resolve sets the system property amie.amp.dir from --amp, or to the user's data folder when AMIE_AMP_DIR is not set, then reads getDirectory() in AmpDirectory.kt. That value is a lazy top-level val: the folder is fixed for the life of the process, which is why the prompt refuses to change it. It sets DJL_CACHE_DIR to AMP/cache/djl and runs ModelsMigration.runOnce, which renames the old modules/, textModels/ and speech folders into models/intents, models/text and models/speech once. The rest of the layout is made lazily by whatever first needs it.
  5. Standard input. HeadlessAmie.readInputFromStandardInput makes a script's input() read from stdin.
  6. Dispatch. A Script goes through ScriptRun.readScript: the file, else a project's main.kts under AMP/projects/<name>, else a starter or saved template by its title. passArguments puts the arguments in the system property amie.args. runCode applies -e through EnvPlan.withEnv, which rewrites or inserts the script's environment(SettingsEnv("...")) line, then calls HeadlessAmie.run.
  7. Compiling and running. HeadlessAmie.run makes AMP/pluginDir and calls ScriptRunner.run in C/script/ScriptRuntime.kt:
  8. EnvPlan.scan, a regex pass over the text, reads the env name and profile and every implementation("g:a:v") or .jar line.
  9. ScriptEnvironments.open(name, profile) returns the env (a global map, and ScriptEnvironments.current), and source(plan) brings its packages: nothing when AMP/env/<name>/env.lock.json already lists the same declarations and every file exists; otherwise the resolver fetches from Maven Central and Google into the shared cache AMP/env/caches/modules-2/files-2.1, copies jars into env/<name>/libs, and rewrites the lock.
  10. env.classLoader(parent) is a cached URLClassLoader over the env's jars.
  11. ScriptEngineCache.engineFor(loader) returns the kts JSR-223 engine, Kotlin's kotlin-scripting-jsr223 with the embeddable compiler: one engine for the app loader, one per env loader, kept for the process.
  12. A SandboxLogger(env, engine, scope) is bound as logger.
  13. assembleScript(code) builds the text that is really compiled: the script's own imports moved up, the default imports (LogLevel, Tensor, ScriptLogger), val amie = bindings["logger"] as ScriptLogger, the prelude from SandboxApi.entries (one fun initMod(...) = amie.initMod(...) per API entry), a SettingsEnv(...) factory, then the body with its import lines blanked so line numbers still match. ScriptErrors.headerLines remembers the header's length to map errors back.
  14. The text is written to AMP/pluginDir/assembly.kts and evaluated with the env's class loader as the context loader, inside ScriptRuns.track(code), which names the run (main.kts, or a template's name) and owns what it opens. Errors become console lines with the script's line and column.
  15. After the script. HeadlessAmie.awaitBackground waits for template runs the script started (a group asked in the background, a template run), telling those waiting on input that none is coming. Serving.waitWhileListening keeps the process up while ModelServer.anyListening, with a shutdown hook that stops the servers.
  16. Shutdown. HeadlessAmie.close, in the finally of Main.kt, closes the databases and the package jars and flushes the log file. Model sessions are not closed one by one; the process exit ends them.

docs.title: A line typed at the prompt
docs.text:
The prompt is not the script path with a loop around it. Repl.start reads lines with JLine (history in ~/.amie_history) or, on a pipe, with readLine(). ReplInput.feed turns a :word line into a command, amie ... into a command line run in-process, and keeps collecting a block until ConsoleBlocks.complete says it parses. Repl.runCode installs a SIGINT handler that calls HeadlessAmie.interruptLines, then HeadlessAmie.runLine, which is TemplateRuns.startLine(code).await():

  • C/script/BackgroundTemplates.kt: startLine makes a TemplateRun marked typed, after refuseWithoutRoom checks the number of runs and the memory the line's models would need (ScriptScan.scan names the models, readModule their encoders). A typed line is a run so that it is listed in sessions, stoppable with Ctrl-C or :terminate, metered, and owns what it opens.
  • ConsoleSession.eval runs it on the one shared interpreter: a kts engine of its own on a daemon thread amie-console (the compiler's state is tied to a thread), opened once with the assembled header evaluated, and kept with its bindings so that what one line defines the next line sees. :reset retires it. A change of env or class loader retires it too, with a line saying what was forgotten.
  • Typed lines never go through EnvPlan.scan: environment(...) typed at the prompt sources nothing; :env name does.

docs.title: What initMod("name") does
docs.text:
ScriptLogger.initMod in C/script/ScriptLogger.kt, in order: a .jar name opens a package through JarPackages.open; a name that is a speech model (SpeechModels.has, a folder of AMP/models/speech) opens through the speech package jar; one in AMP/models/imported with a model that runs here (ImportedModels.has) opens through ONNX Runtime or DJL (an encoder_model.onnx with decoder_model.onnx pair as EncoderDecoderModel: two sessions, encode making the encoder's input from text or, through preprocessor_config.json, a sound or image file, and the greedy loop left to the script); a path does the same; everything else is an intent or text model, ModelSessions.acquire(name):

  1. One session per model name, global and synchronized; an open one is reused.
  2. InitMod(name).moduleModel reads AMP/models/intents/<name>/module.json through AmpModules.readModule, checks ModelRequirements.blockers, opens the head model.onnx as an ONNX Runtime session and takes the encoder from SharedEncoders.acquire: one BertOnnxModel per encoder path, reference-counted, closed by the last release.
  3. BundledModels.root is where the encoder lives: amie.models.dir, AMIE_MODELS_DIR, else AMP/models/bert with the bge encoder in bge/. scripts/setup.sh downloads both.
  4. OrtScopes.opened registers the session with an enclosing ortClosable { } block when there is one, and ScriptRuns.opened("model:<id>") records it on the run, which is what :sessions lists and :terminate closes.

modelBuilder(name, data) is SandboxLogger.modelBuilder → parseLabeledData → JetBuilder.buildClassifier: preprocess, embed through the encoder (cache in AMP/cache/embeddings), train and score candidate heads, validate and optionally calibrate, export. AmpModules.writeModule writes AMP/models/intents/<name>/model.onnx, module.json and the guide, keeps the previous head under versions/, updates modules.json, and swaps the open sessions and listeners when it is a retrain; ModuleMetrics.appendMetrics writes metrics.json and refreshes the model card.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text: C/ResponseDto.kt defines the line: time, message, level (INFO, ERROR, DATA, INTERNAL), source (sandbox/main.kts, internal, ...). logToConsole in C/console/ConsoleLog.kt hands it to the installed console, keeps the last 200 error lines for errorLog(), appends it to AMP/logs.txt on one writer thread (rotating past 20 MB), and for an ERROR offers it to ErrorReporter, which does nothing without a signed-in user. logInternal is the same at the INTERNAL level, which Output.print drops unless -v or a command asks for it.

docs.title: The AMP folder
docs.text:
Everything amie reads and writes is under one folder, the same one the desktop app uses: --amp DIR, else AMIE_AMP_DIR, else ~/Library/Application Support/amie pilot/AMP on a Mac, %APPDATA%\amie pilot\AMP on Windows, $XDG_DATA_HOME/amie-pilot/AMP or ~/.local/share/amie-pilot/AMP elsewhere.

Folder or file Holds Made by models/bert/, models/bert/bge/ the NER model and the encoder every intent model is trained on scripts/setup.sh models/intents/<name>/ the trained intent models: model.onnx, module.json, metrics.json, guide.md, versions/; intents/modules.json is the registry modelBuilder models/text/<name>/ the chat models, ONNX Runtime GenAI exports hf import of a GenAI repo models/speech/<name>/ Whisper and the voices the speech package runs hf import of a Piper voice, or by hand models/imported/<name>/ any other model of the Hub or copied in, with its source.json hf import, huggingFace() env/<name>/ an env: env.lock.json, libs/, groups.json; env/caches/ the shared Maven cache envs new, a script's environment(...) templates/ the starters and saved scripts amie examples, templates projects/<name>/main.kts a project amie new pluginDir/ package jars, assembly.kts (the last assembled script), runs.jsonl, config/speech/ the engine cache/embeddings/, cache/djl/ encoder outputs between builds; DJL's native libraries the builder, DJL logs.txt every console line, at every level logToConsole

docs.title: Settings the engine reads
docs.text: Environment variables: AMIE_AMP_DIR, AMIE_MODELS_DIR, DJL_CACHE_DIR, HF_TOKEN (a private Hub repo), AMIE_JAVA_HOME and JAVA_HOME (the launcher), AMIE_BUILD (the checkout script), AMIE_BACKEND_URL and AMIE_SITE_URL (the jar fetch). System properties set at run time: amie.amp.dir, DJL_CACHE_DIR, amie.args and the slf4j levels; read: amie.version, amie.models.dir, compose.application.resources.dir (the app's bundle, never set here), user.dir, user.home.

docs.title: Things to know before changing the engine
docs.text:
• Global state. The console, the current env and the env map, the engine cache, the shared interpreter, the model sessions, the shared encoders, the ONNX scopes and the runs are all process-wide singletons. Tests that touch them must run one JVM at a time, and amie's tests point AMIE_AMP_DIR at build/test-amp.
  • AMIE_AMP_DIR beats --amp. getDirectory() reads the environment variable before the property that --amp sets.
  • The AMP folder cannot change inside a process, see step 4.
  • A refused prompt line ends the prompt. refuseWithoutRoom throws when memory is short or too many runs are open, and nothing between it and Amie.main catches it.
  • Two readers of standard input. On a pipe the prompt reads lines with readLine(), while a script's input() reads its own buffered reader of System.in.
  • A developer path remains in BundledModels, the last candidate for the encoder folder.
  • Imports keep a repo's layout except chat models and voices, which land flat; the imported scan looks six folders deep.

docs.title: The components
docs.text:
The pieces every page is built from, each in a file of its own under amieApplication/desktopApp/src/main/kotlin/org/example/project/components/ui/viewport/. Use one of these before drawing anything of your own: a page that needs a button, a menu, a hint, a fold or a two-pane layout takes it from here, so every page looks and behaves the same. The pictures come from ui/ComponentShotsTest.kt, which draws each family with plain data (AMIE_COMPONENT_SHOTS=<dir> writes them; the test runs without it).

The rules they all follow are in LONG_RUN_PROMPT.md, Appendix C: flat, square (4px corners), muted colours from ui/theme/Color.kt, a tooltip on every control, text with a capital first letter and never in capitals.

docs.title: Colour
docs.text:
Every colour is a token of ui/theme/Color.kt; no page names one of its own. The chrome is neutral gray, three steps darker than the JetBrains dark theme, and three hues sit on it as accents, never as floods:

Token Hue For AccentColor (PageAccent, AddButton) Dark blue The fill of the one primary action per place, light words on it (OnPrimaryColor) AccentInk (AccentLine, FocusRingColor, TabActiveIndicator, PanelEdgeSelected, ActiveColor, LinkColor) Blue Lines and words that mark what is chosen, focused or under way: the focus ring, a focused field's border, the open tab's bar, a selected row's edge, a link, the line of a build or a download AccentWash (PanelSurfaceSelected, CompletionSelected) Blue, faint What is selected sits on it: a row, the open page in the sidebar, the lit line of a list; EditorSelection is the editor's own, a step stronger SuccessColor (RunIconColor) Green What runs, succeeded or is done: a status mark, the Run icon, the bar of a notice that ended well DangerColor (StopIconColor, the DangerButton tones) Red What ends, removes or failed

A hover is a gray shade (HoverOverlay, SurfaceHover), never the wash: blue says chosen, not pointed at. ContrastTest holds every pair in use (words 4.5:1, marks 3:1) and checks that the accents are blue and green and the chrome's grays neutral, so a colour used on a new surface is added there.

docs.title: Buttons and switches: Controls.kt
docs.text:
Component For Use it when AccentButton(label, tip) { } The one primary action of a place: Build, Run, Save. The only filled button, dark blue A place has one action that matters most; never two accents side by side SecondaryButton(label, tip) { } The neutral action beside an accent or a danger button: Cancel, Keep The person can back out, or there is a second way that changes nothing DangerButton(label, tip) { } What ends or removes something: Terminate, Delete, Destroy. Outlined in red The action cannot be undone or ends a session; the menus colour the same words red SmallButton(label, tip, icon, arrow) { } The small ghost button for everything else: Validate, Add, Show the rows An action of a row or a header; arrow = true when it opens a menu CloseButton(tip) { } The ✕ that closes a panel or a form; an ordinary ghost, never red Closing ends nothing Toggle(label, on, tip) { } What is on or off: Keep texts, Serve A setting with two states; outlined draws a border where it stands alone IconChip(icon, tip) { }, AccentIconButton(icon, tip) { } A small square with only an icon: the sandbox's Run, Stop and export (16px outlined icons, iconSize = 16.dp), a filter's clear There is no room for a word and the tip says what it does

A button whose work is running reads as its own word with an ellipsis, Building…, is disabled until it is done and draws the loading dots after the word (BusyLabel, in Loading.kt).

docs.title: Menus: Menus.kt
docs.text:
Component For Use it when MenuBox(items) { close } The dark box with one line per action, the ending ones (Terminate, Delete, Remove, Stop, Detach) in red A right-click or a ⋯ opens the actions of an item; MENU_HEADING starts a line that only names a group DropButton(label, items, tip) A button that opens a MenuBox under itself, right edges aligned (BelowButton) A list of things to pick from, as the sandbox's Examples MoreButton(items) (in Panels.kt) The ⋯ at the right of a detail header, with the same actions a right-click opens A detail panel has actions beyond its buttons

A page that wants the keyboard back after a menu closes gives a MenuWatcher through LocalMenuWatcher.

docs.title: Tooltips: Tooltip.kt
docs.text: AppTooltip(text) { content } shows a short explanation under the pointer after it rests half a second on the content: what a button does, or what a tab holds. Every control above takes its tip and wraps itself in one; use it directly for anything else that needs a word, such as a status dot or a tab. A null text shows the content as it is.

docs.title: Text pieces: Texts.kt
docs.text: Component For Use it when Hint(text) One muted line that says what is going on or what to do: "No models yet; Build makes one" A list or pane has nothing to show, or something needs a word of guidance Meta(text) One small muted line of facts: when it was built, on how many rows Facts under a name or a title Para(text) A paragraph of the guide in the ordinary text colour Explaining something in full sentences Lines(vararg lines) A few lines a script would hold, in the console's box so they can be selected and copied Showing code the person may copy KeyValues(pairs, tips, varying) Aligned key: value lines in monospace; keys in varying are marked as of this run Details of a model or a session BadgeLabel(text, strong) A small label on a faint square: Served, v3, Calibrated A state worth a glance in a list row Modifier.variesByRun() Marks what differs from run to run, so a screenshot compare skips it A time, a count or a memory figure in a page the harness photographs

docs.title: Sections and folds: Sections.kt
docs.text: Component For Use it when Fold(title, count, open, key) { } A section that opens on click: chevron, title and count in the header Content worth hiding by default, as the sandbox's Recent runs; openNow opens it from elsewhere Section(title, key, actions) { } A block of a detail tab: the title on a line that folds it away (open by default), a rule, the content A tab holds several blocks, each with a name FormHeader(hint, onClose) The first line of a form: what the form does and the ✕ that leaves it A form opens inside a page, as New model does

docs.title: Fields: Fields.kt
docs.text: Component For Use it when SearchField(value, tip, list, name) { } A one-line filter over a list: icon, text and a clear button once there is text A list is long enough to filter; list = true for the one ⌘F reaches SettingField(label, value, tip, masked) { } A labelled one-line input: Host, Port, a key (masked) A setting the person types NoMatches(query) { clear } Says a filter left nothing, with the query, and clears it Under a filtered list that is empty

docs.title: Panels and the detail layout: Panels.kt
docs.text: Component For Use it when DetailPanel { } The bordered panel of the selected item, at the right of a list A page is a list and the detail of what is selected (Models, Packages, Sessions, Settings) DetailHeader(name, active, status, statusTip, menu) { actions } Name and status on the left, the actions on the right (or under, when narrow), then the ⋯ menu The first thing in a DetailPanel StatusMark(active, tip) A 7dp dot: green while active, gray when not A row or a header says whether something runs ListRow (in Panels.kt) A row of a list: its icon, name, meta line and status; selected, it sits on the blue wash with a blue edge Every list of the Models page VerticalSeparator(onWidth) The rule between the list and the detail, dragged to change the split Between the two panes

docs.title: Dialogs: Dialogs.kt
docs.text:
Component For Use it when ConfirmBox(title, confirm, onConfirm, onKeep, text, keep) A question that stands in the page, under what it is about: Keep first, the action last Before anything that cannot be undone DialogCard(title, text) { buttons } The shared card: a title, a line under it, the buttons at the right Any message that stops the person ErrorDialog(title, message, onDismiss) The card floating over the window with one OK An error the person must see before going on

They share one width (DialogWidth), one title line and one button height, checked by ui/DialogShotsTest.kt.

docs.title: Loading: Loading.kt
docs.text:
The one way the app waits. Nothing in it shows before about 150 ms have gone by, so a fast read never flickers.

Component For Use it when Loading(text) The place of a pane or a list that is still reading: the dots and words saying what is waited for State that starts null or empty and is filled by a LaunchedEffect or a poll; a list says "Reading the models…" until its first read, never "No models yet" LoadingContent(loading, text) { } Crossfades from the wait to the content once it is there A pane whose content replaces the wait in one piece BusyLabel(label, color) A button's or a row's label while it works, the dots alive after the word The four text buttons draw their label with it: a label that starts with an -ing word and ends in … ("Opening…", "Reading the queue…") is busy by itself. Any other ellipsis says a dialog follows ("Fine-tune on file…", "Export…") and is drawn still (isBusyLabel) LoadingDots(color, size) The dots alone A line of the console (its last line while the run is busy, when it ends in …) or a strip ProgressLine(fraction, color) The thin two-dp line of a run or a build: filled to fraction, or sweeping when the work can't say how far it is Under the console strip, the build line of the Models list, a package being added

Every wait in the app uses these: the lists of the Models page before their first snapshot, the sandbox's editor and Recent runs before their files are read, the console while a text model loads or the builder embeds and fits, the settings' file tree, the package repository's search, and the window before the sandbox has taken over.

docs.title: The frame of the window
docs.text:
Component File For NavigationSidebar(...) NavigationSidebar.kt The column at the left of every page: the sandbox, the models page, the settings gear and the page's own tools, each a SidebarItem with its tip WindowHeader(name, onBack) { tools } WindowHeader.kt The window's top bar, which is the page's toolbar: back, the page's tools (the sandbox's script and Run, the Models tabs, the Settings sections), an optional add button and the window controls (on a Mac room for the system's three instead); it is the drag area, with no title. BarTab is a tab in it StatusStrip() StatusStrip.kt The strip at the foot: the process's memory, the heap and the encoders in memory, read every two seconds while it shows ThinScrollbar(scroll) ThinScrollbar.kt The thin bar at the side of what scrolls, dim until the pointer is on it Modifier.tracksFocusVisibility, FocusRing FocusRing.kt The 1dp ring a control shows while the keyboard put the focus on it LocalAppChrome AppChrome.kt What the window gives the header: the drag area, the window controls, and systemControls when the system draws its own

The lists of the device dashboard (DataEntryList.kt, EndpointEntryList.kt, DevicePanel.kt) are of that page alone and are not reused.

docs.title: Beyond the viewport
docs.text:
• Helpers under components/terminal/window/controller/util/: Desktop.kt (chooseFile, openInBrowser, openFile) and Numbers.kt (fmt, pct) are the plain functions pages share; they draw nothing.
  • The console (console/), sessions (modules/ModelSessions.kt, tabs/SessionsTab.kt) and the script API (initMod, sessionMod, ortClosable in script/ScriptLogger.kt) are documented where they live, with KDoc on every member a script can call; Scripting API lists them for a script writer.

docs.title: Cookbook: scripts to copy
docs.text:
Every script on this page runs as it is in the sandbox: paste it into main.kts, press Run (⌘↵), read the console. The shorter versions are one click away in the app: the disk icon on the strip over the editor (templates) lists them as starter templates and Load puts one in the editor (your own script is kept under AMP/pluginDir/backup/). Nothing here needs an account; the one call that does, saveState, says so. They are ordered from the first thing to try to the things you will do once a model exists. The exact signatures are in the Scripting API; this page is about what to type.

One habit that saves time: open a model or a database once at the top of the script and keep it open between runs (see Running sessions). The first run loads, every later run is instant.

docs.title: 1. Logging: four levels, four toggles
docs.text:
log("plain line")                       // info: the script's own output
info("same as log")
data("rows: 3, columns: text,label")    // data: what the script produced, kept apart from chatter
error("something is off")               // error: red, and the error toggle turns on by itself when a run fails
log("explicit", LogLevel.INTERNAL)      // internal: what the app itself says (sessions, builds, env); LogLevel is in scope
  • The console shows info only when the app starts; the other three toggles on the console strip have counts, so error 1 means one line is waiting behind a toggle. all turns everything on.
  • Everything, whatever the toggles, goes to AMP/logs.txt.
  • Every inference of a model is also a data line (dummy "sunny" -> lights 0.671, weather 0.496, …), so data is where to look when a model answers.

docs.title: 2. Ask a model: initMod and its interface
docs.text:
Every fresh AMP/ has a model called dummy (labels greeting, lights, weather), so this runs before anything is trained:

val m = initMod("dummy")                      // the model's session: opened now, or the one already open

log(m.predict("turn the lights on"))          // lights            the label (the argmax)
log(m.scores("turn the lights on").toString()) // {lights=0.67, weather=0.50, greeting=0.33}
m.predictions("hello there").forEach { p -> log("${p.label} ${p.score}") }
m.inference("hello there").forEach { log(it) } // the raw lines: label:score, best first
log(m.getStatus().toString())                 // the manifest: encoder, dims, labels, description

// Leave it open while you iterate, or:
// m.close()

What initMod gives you is an InteractionModel:

Member Returns Use it for predict(text) String The label. Throws when the model answers nothing scores(text) Map<String, Float> Every label with its score, best first; a confidence check predictions(text) List<Prediction> label and score as values, in the model's order inference(text) List<String> The raw answer: label:score for a classifier, a tag per token for NER, whatever run(text) returned for a package getStatus() Any The manifest of a model, the metadata of the NER model, the status map of a package close() Frees the session; the Models page's Terminate does the same

The three forms of initMod:

Call What it opens How many initMod("name") A model exported to AMP/models/intents/<name> One per model. A second call returns the open session initMod("name.jar") A package jar (env, AMP/pluginDir, a path, or fetched from the server) A new instance every call; close what you open initMod() The bundled BERT NER model A plain object you own; close it yourself

A confidence gate, the most common thing to write around scores:

val m = initMod("dummy")
listOf("turn the lights on", "what's the weather", "asdf qwerty").forEach { text ->
    val scores = m.scores(text)
    val (label, score) = scores.entries.first()
    if (score < 0.5f) log("$text -> not sure ($label ${"%.2f".format(score)})")
    else log("$text -> $label ${"%.2f".format(score)}")
}

docs.title: 3. Train your own model from a csv
docs.text:
AMP/sample-intents.csv (45 rows, text,label) is written on first start; any csv with a text column and a label column works (the columns are found by their headers: text, label, intent, …).

val train = source("sample-intents.csv")           // looked up as given, then in AMP/, then AMP/pluginDir/
relate(train, "intents-test.csv")                  // optional: validate on this file instead of a 20% split

val built = modelBuilder("intents", train)         // cleans the rows, embeds them, tries four heads, keeps the best, exports ONNX
built.modelStatus()                                // the validation table: precision, recall, F1 per label
built.modelChart()                                 // the same as ASCII bars, the build history, the confusion matrix

val m = initMod("intents")
log(m.predict("switch off the kitchen light"))     // lights

Before building, checkData(train) prints what the preprocessor would clean, drop and refuse, and whether a build could start. The console tells you what the preprocessor did to the rows (what it dropped and why), how every candidate head scored, which one was kept, and what the validation says about it (a head that memorises, one that barely beats the majority label, labels it confuses). When the data cannot give a classifier the build stops with the reason in red (label 'weather' has 3 rows after cleaning, at least 5 are needed…); the reasons and what to do about each are in Models and metrics. Your own heads instead of the four defaults:

val train = source("sample-intents.csv")
val options = buildOptions(
    candidates = listOf(
        architecture(hidden = listOf(32, 16), epochs = 200, learningRate = 0.005),
        architecture(hidden = emptyList(), epochs = 100),             // a linear head
        architecture(hidden = listOf(64), activation = "Tanh"),
    ),
    pickBy = "accuracy",
    balanceClasses = true,          // a rare label weighs as much as a frequent one
    seed = 7,                       // the same data and seed always give the same model
)
val built = modelBuilder("intents-custom", train, options)
built.modelStatus()

Later, without rebuilding:

validateMetrics("intents")                         // the stored validation
metricsChart("intents", labels = listOf("lights")) // one label's bars
metricsHistory("intents")                          // accuracy and macro F1 across builds
confusionMatrix("intents")

The build's phases and progress show on the console strip; the Models page lists the model with its metrics as plots once it is exported. What happens inside: Building a model.

docs.title: 4. Named entities: initAmie and initMod()
docs.text:
Both use the bundled BERT NER model (people, organisations, places, misc). initAmie opens and closes the model for one text, so it is the right call for a one-off; initMod() keeps it open for many texts.

val tags = initAmie("Angela Merkel met Tim Cook in Berlin")   // printed, and returned: one tag per token
log(tags.joinToString(" "))                                    // O B-PER I-PER O B-PER I-PER O B-LOC O

val ner = initMod()                                            // the same model, kept open
listOf("Apple opened a store in Paris", "Marie Curie worked in Warsaw").forEach { text ->
    log("$text -> ${ner.inference(text).joinToString(" ")}")
}
ner.close()                                                    // not listed on the Models page, so close it here

The tags line up with the tokenizer's tokens: [CLS] and [SEP] at the ends (always O) and one tag per word piece, so a name split into Mer and ##kel gets B-PER and I-PER. The token ids of a text come from forwardContext(text) { ids -> … } when you need to line them up yourself.

docs.title: 5. Embeddings: forwardContext
docs.text:
forwardContext runs the encoder and returns the hidden state [batch][token][hidden]. Mean-pool it to get one vector per text; that is exactly what modelBuilder feeds its head with.

fun embed(text: String): FloatArray? {
    val hidden = forwardContext(text) { ids -> log("${ids.size} tokens", LogLevel.INTERNAL) } ?: return null
    val tokens = hidden[0]                                 // [token][hidden]
    val dim = tokens[0].size
    return FloatArray(dim) { i -> tokens.sumOf { it[i].toDouble() }.toFloat() / tokens.size }
}

fun cosine(a: FloatArray, b: FloatArray): Double {
    var dot = 0.0; var na = 0.0; var nb = 0.0
    for (i in a.indices) { dot += a[i] * b[i]; na += a[i] * a[i]; nb += b[i] * b[i] }
    return dot / (Math.sqrt(na) * Math.sqrt(nb))
}

val lights = embed("turn the lights on")!!
listOf("switch the lamp off", "will it rain tomorrow", "good morning").forEach { text ->
    log("$text -> ${"%.3f".format(cosine(lights, embed(text)!!))}")
}

forwardContext returns null (with an Error line) when the text is blank or the encoder failed.

docs.title: 6. Any ONNX model: importModelOnnx
docs.text:
A model file with the same inference / getStatus / close interface. A transformer (an input_ids input) needs tokenizer.json next to it; labels come from a config.json (id2label) next to it when there is one; a model with one float input takes the text as comma-separated numbers.

val m = importModelOnnx("/Users/me/models/sentiment/model.onnx")
if (m == null) {
    error("the model could not be opened; the console says why")
} else {
    log(m.getStatus().toString())                          // inputs, outputs, labels, producer
    log(m.predict("what a great day"))                     // POSITIVE
    m.scores("what a great day").forEach { (label, p) -> log("$label ${"%.3f".format(p)}") }
    m.close()
}

Its session appears under ORT sessions (sessions.print()), not on the Models page.

docs.title: 7. Sessions: see what is open, close what you don't need
docs.text:
sessions.print()                         // every ONNX Runtime session: name, inputs, outputs, runs, busy or not
packages.print()                         // the open package instances
ortSessions().forEach { log(it) }        // the same as sessions.print(), as a list

sessions.cancel("module:dummy")          // ends that ORT session and what runs on it; the model opens it again on its next text
packages.closeAll()                      // every package instance this or any script opened
sessions.cancelAll()                     // everything, encoders included; open models load them again on their next text

A build, a fine-tune or texts to label running texts through an encoder stops at a cancel of it, also one that lands between two of its texts; one started after the cancel runs as usual.

A model has one session at most, so running a script ten times does not pile up ten copies. Packages are the opposite: every initMod("x.jar") is a new instance, so a script that opens one should close it, or start with packages.closeAll().

sessionMod("name") is a model to ask and nothing more, a snapshot of the head it has now: it can't train or change the model, writes nothing to its log, needs nothing else open and stays on that head through a fine-tune.

val m = sessionMod("dummy")             // goes when the run ends, or with m.close()
log(m.predict("turn the lights on"))
log("v${m.version}: ${m.labels}")

val label = sessionMod("dummy") {       // for one block: the model's functions at hand, gone when it ends
    log(scores("turn the lights on").toString())
    predict("turn the lights on")        // what the call returns
}
log(label)

The Sessions tab lists it as a Session model, and over the sessions Scripts: what each script running holds and has used. More in Running sessions.

docs.title: 8. Packages: jars with run(text) and close()
docs.text:
packages.available().forEach { log("${it.name} ${it.version ?: ""}") }   // what the server offers
packages.fetch("amie-demo-1.0.0.jar")                                     // into AMP/pluginDir; null if not there

val echo = runCatching { initMod("amie-demo-1.0.0.jar") }      // a new instance in its own class loader
    .onFailure { error("package not opened: ${it.message}") }   // not found anywhere, or no class with run(String)/close()
    .getOrNull()
if (echo != null) {
    try {
        echo.run("hello there").forEach { log(it) }   // echo.answer("...") is the first answer
        log(echo.getStatus().toString())             // id, jar, class, source, url, page, runs
    } finally {
        echo.close()
    }
}

A jar that only has a static entry point (run() or main) is a plugin, run once with importPlugin; nothing is opened, nothing to close:

importPlugin("tools.jar")                    // never throws: what its run() returned, or the failure, is one console line

Building a package of your own: Building a package.

docs.title: 9. A library from Maven Central
docs.text:
Declare it at the top (the line is read before the script compiles), then import as usual. The Models page's Add → From Maven Central… does the same with a search box.

implementation("com.google.code.gson:gson:2.11.0")
import com.google.gson.GsonBuilder

val gson = GsonBuilder().setPrettyPrinting().create()
val m = initMod("dummy")
val answer = mapOf("text" to "turn the lights on", "scores" to m.scores("turn the lights on"))
log(gson.toJson(answer))

The env keeps what was ever imported (internalEnv() prints it), so the second run downloads nothing. A dependency("…") is another name for implementation; environment(SettingsEnv("name", "profile")) selects another env.

docs.title: 10. Remember something between runs: saveState and loadState
docs.text:
The sandbox has no variables that outlive a run. saveState keeps a JSON text under a name on the Amie backend, per signed-in user, so it follows you to another machine and survives a fresh AMP/; think "the labels I settled on", "the last csv I used", "my serving port". A local file does the same thing without signing in.

// On the backend (signed in): one JSON document per name
saveState("intents-config", """{"model": "intents", "threshold": 0.6}""")
listStates().forEach { log(it) }                       // devices, intents-config, …
val config = loadState("intents-config")               // the text, or null when there is none (or not signed in)
log(config ?: "nothing saved yet")

// Locally: a file of your own
val file = java.io.File(System.getProperty("user.home"), "intents-config.json")
file.writeText("""{"threshold": 0.6}""")
log(file.readText())

A failure (a guest, an unreachable backend, a bad name) is one Error line and loadState returns null, so a script can fall back:

val threshold = loadState("intents-config")?.substringAfter("\"threshold\": ")?.substringBefore("}")?.toFloatOrNull() ?: 0.5f

docs.title: 11. Postgres: database("main")
docs.text:
The connections live in AMP/databases.json, written with one main entry the first time anything asks for it. Edit it (the file is not committed to git):

{
  "main": {
    "url": "jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/postgres",
    "user": "postgres",
    "password": "$ENV:PGPASSWORD",
    "description": "the local one"
  },
  "warehouse": { "url": "jdbc:postgresql://db.example.com:5432/analytics", "user": "amie", "password": "$ENV:WAREHOUSE_PW" }
}

$ENV:NAME is read from the environment variable NAME when the connection opens, so the file holds no secret. Then, in a script:

databases.print()                                       // every entry: url, user, open or not
val db = database("main")                               // the same object for the same name while the app runs

db.tables().forEach { log(it) }                         // public.messages, …
db.print("select id, text from messages order by id desc limit 10")      // a table in the console (data lines)

val rows = db.query("select text from messages where label is null limit ?", 50)   // ? placeholders, in order
val m = initMod("intents")
rows.forEach { row ->
    val text = row["text"].toString()
    db.execute("update messages set label = ?, score = ? where text = ?", m.predict(text), m.scores(text).values.first(), text)
}
log("labeled ${rows.size} rows; ${db.scalar("select count(*) from messages where label is null")} left")
Call Returns Notes query(sql, params…) List<Map<String, Any?>> One map per row, columns in the query's order; values as JDBC gives them (Int, String, java.sql.Timestamp, …) scalar(sql, params…) Any? The first column of the first row execute(sql, params…) Int Rows touched by INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE, 0 for DDL print(sql, params…) the rows Also prints them as a table, at most 200 rows tables() List<String> schema.table, system schemas left out close() The app closes open connections on exit; databases.closeAll() closes every one now

Every failure is one Error line (database 'main': relation "messages" does not exist [42P01] in: select …) and a DatabaseException the script can catch:

val db = database("main")
try {
    db.execute("create table if not exists predictions (text text, label text, score real, at timestamptz default now())")
    db.execute("insert into predictions (text, label, score) values (?, ?, ?)", "hi", "greeting", 0.91f)
} catch (e: Exception) {
    error("database: ${e.message}")      // a bad host, a wrong password, a typo in the SQL: all land here
}

A wrong host or password shows as database 'main': can't connect to jdbc:postgresql://… as 'postgres': … on the first statement, not when database("main") is called.

docs.title: 12. Serve a model and call it over HTTP
docs.text:
A served model answers POST {"text": "…"} (or a plain-text body) and GET ?text=… at its predict URL with {"model": "intents", "predictions": [{"label": "lights", "score": 0.97}, …]}. The Models page's Listen does it with a switch; a script does it with serve:

val url = serve("dummy", port = 8765)               // http://127.0.0.1:8765/models/dummy/predict; null if it could not start
    ?: throw IllegalStateException("serve did not start; the console says why: port taken, path served already, model can't load")
log("serving at $url")
log(servingUrl("dummy") ?: "not serving")            // the same URL while it listens

// Call it from the script, with the errors handled
import java.net.URI
import java.net.http.HttpClient
import java.net.http.HttpRequest
import java.net.http.HttpResponse

val http = HttpClient.newHttpClient()
fun ask(text: String): String {
    val request = HttpRequest.newBuilder(URI.create(url))
        .header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        .POST(HttpRequest.BodyPublishers.ofString("""{"text": "$text"}"""))
        .build()
    return try {
        val response = http.send(request, HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString())
        when (response.statusCode()) {
            200 -> response.body()
            400 -> "no text in the request: ${response.body()}"          // {"error": "send text as {\"text\": ...}"}
            405 -> "method not allowed: ${response.body()}"               // the methods list excludes it
            500 -> "the model failed: ${response.body()}"                 // inference threw; also counted as an error on the page
            else -> "unexpected ${response.statusCode()}: ${response.body()}"
        }
    } catch (e: java.net.ConnectException) {
        "nothing listens at $url (${e.message})"
    } catch (e: Exception) {
        "request failed: ${e.message}"
    }
}

log(ask("turn the lights on"))
log(ask(""))                                        // 400
stopServing("dummy")                                // and it stays off on the next start

Every request is appended to AMP/models/intents/<name>/incoming.jsonl and counted on the Models page. Host, port, path, methods and a min score passed to serve are saved to serving.json, so the page shows them; serve("dummy") with no arguments reuses whatever the page saved. The HTTP side is described in Serving a model.

A client that sees a wrong answer can correct the model over the same port and have it retrained while it keeps answering, with the new head swapped in when it is ready:

val base = url.removeSuffix("/predict")
fun send(method: String, route: String, body: String? = null): String {
