An encoder counts once however many share it answers What those sessions answered cpu, allocated The CPU time and the bytes allocated on the script's own thread, kept from the end of the run on. Threads the script starts and ONNX Runtime's own aren't in them, and allocated isn't memory held: most of it is garbage soon

Each session has a resources line of its own under its row:

dummy  #3          intent model · 14 runs · 2m 10s
head 9 KB · encoder 415.6 MB, shared by 3 · 12 ms a run · last used 3s ago
Kind What its line says Intent model, session model head, the model's ONNX head on disk; encoder, the encoder folder it runs on, said once with how many open sessions share it (shared by 3), left out while that encoder isn't loaded; the time a run takes on average; when it was last used Package jar, the jar on disk; the time a call takes; when it was last used ONNX session file, the bare ONNX file; the time a run takes inside ONNX Runtime; when it was last used Model group heads, its members' heads together; their encoder once; the time a run of the swarm takes; when it was last used Background template What its run meter reads right now, the figures the console prints when it ends: memory 1.20 GB, peak 1.40 GB · heap 340.0 MB of 4.00 GB · cpu 2.10 s · ort 12 runs in 640 ms (of the whole process; what each figure is, in The output console)

A session that hasn't run yet has no time and no last use. Over the rows, one line sums the tab up:

Process 1.85 GB, of which encoders 415.6 MB · heap 340.0 MB of 4.00 GB · 20 sessions weigh 436.0 MB

What the process holds of the machine's memory (from the same reading as the status strip at the foot of the window), how much of that is the encoders loaded outside the heap, the heap against its -Xmx limit, and what the open sessions weigh together: each one's own file and every encoder once. File sizes are read as the page polls; they are one look at the file each, the same look that tells whether it changed.

The starter What a script uses asks a model for 30 seconds, so there is time to open the tab and watch it.

docs.title: What runs where
docs.text:
• inference blocks the script until the answer is back. The model work itself runs on the app's ONNX threads, never on the UI thread, so the window stays responsive while a script waits.
  • One text at a time goes through a model's encoder. Two scripts asking the same model take turns; the Sessions tab shows inferring while a call is in flight.
  • Only one script runs at a time. Pressing Run during a run logs Script is already running; the sessions a running script opened stay open after it ends, whether it finished or failed.
  • A script cannot be stopped from the window. Terminating the session it is using makes its next inference throw Model <name> (#id) is closed, which ends the script with Failed after ….
  • Serving (Listen on the Models page) and Validate do not use your session: Listen loads its own instance of the model and closes it on Stop; a validation opens a session for its run, logs every row to it, and closes it at the end. Terminating a session never stops a listener.
  • A new head of the model (a fine-tune, a build under the same name, a rollback, a client's /retrain) doesn't close your session: the new head is opened beside the one answering, put in its place once the answers in flight are done, and the old one is closed after. The session keeps its id, its run count and its log, which gets a swap line (head v1 → v2 (fine-tune) swapped in; the head before was closed once its answers were done); a script holding it just gets the new head's answers from then on, and a swarm over it too. A listener swaps the same way, on the same port. Only a model that stops keeping texts closes its session instead. A sessionMod doesn't move: it stays on the head it was taken on.
  • A model's encoder (the BERT part, hundreds of MB) is loaded once and shared by every session, listener, build and validation on the same encoder folder; it is closed when the last of them closes. Cancelling an ONNX Runtime session (sessions.cancel, sessions.cancelAll(), Terminate all) ends what was running on it and frees it, but doesn't break the models using it: a model session or a listener whose head or encoder was cancelled opens it again on its next text, so only the call that was running when the cancel came fails.

docs.title: Close sessions
docs.text:
Call or button What it ends m.close() this session; a second call does nothing The end of an ortClosable block what that block opened itself, the last opened first, after the templates it started have ended (Scope functions) ortScopes.free("name"), ortScopes.freeAll() what that static, required or limited scope holds, what every one of them holds An ortRequired scope with nothing else in session what it holds, once no other session is open One more than max opened in an ortLimited scope the oldest it holds packages.closeAll() every open package session (each package's close() is called, its class loader dropped) sessions.cancel("module:intents"), sessions.cancel("3") ONNX Runtime sessions by name or id; in-flight runs are terminated first. The model it belonged to stays open and opens it again on its next text sessions.cancelAll() every ONNX Runtime session, including the heads of open models and the shared encoder; open models and listeners open what they need again on their next text m.close() on a sessionMod, the end of its block or of the run this hold of the snapshot; the last to let go closes it Terminate on the Sessions tab (also on a model's or package's own panel), or in the sandbox's Still open tab that session; on a session model the snapshot, for all who hold it Free on a session's row (Sessions tab and Still open tab), for one a kept scope holds what that scope holds, as ortScopes.free("name") does Terminate all on the Sessions tab, Free all in the Still open tab everything open: swarms, model sessions, session models, package sessions, ONNX sessions, and every template running in the background free name, free all, terminate #3, terminate name, terminate all typed into the sandbox's console the same as the buttons, without a script; sessions lists what is open first (The command line) job.cancel(), templateRuns.cancelAll(), Stop in the Templates pane a template running in the background, or all of them

After a close, the session's row disappears, its log file keeps the history, and any further inference on the closed object throws. Sessions do not survive a restart of the app: it starts with none open.

docs.title: When something is off
docs.text: Console says What it means this sessionMod of dummy was closed It was asked after its close() or past the block it was for. Take it again the snapshot of dummy v1 was terminated Terminate ended it for all who held it. Take it again for the head the model has now initMod: 'x' is already open as session #3, that one is used Normal: a model has one session; you got the open one Error: Model x (#3) is closed The session was terminated (Terminate or Terminate all on the page, close()), or the ortClosable block it was opened in has ended; call initMod("x") again ortClosable 'closable': model x #3 was open already, so it is used and left open Normal: a closable frees only what it opened itself initMod: 'x' head was cancelled, opened again as #12 A cancel (sessions.cancel, cancelAll(), Terminate all) ended the model's head; it was opened again for this text encoder: bge was cancelled, opened again as #14 The same for the shared encoder: it opens its ONNX Runtime session again on the next text, for every model holding it Module 'x' not found in …/AMP/models/intents No model of that name was built; see the Models tab or AMP/models/intents/ Module 'x' can't run: head: model.onnx missing in x/; labels: 1 for 2 outputs: a The model lacks something it needs, so nothing of it was opened; the message names all of it. initMod, Open session and Listen refuse when the encoder folder, its model.onnx, tokenizer.json or config.json is missing, when the encoder's hidden size isn't what the head expects, when the head file is missing, or when there isn't one label per output. A config.json with no hidden_size doesn't count, since a DistilBERT config says dim. The model's Requirements tab shows the same lines Package 'x.jar' can't run: key.properties: still its template, fill it in; $API_KEY: not set and required. Its config folder is … The package lacks something its metadata says it needs, so no instance of it was made; the message names all of it and the folder. initMod and Test run refuse when a required config file is missing, when a required one still equals its template (written there on that first open, for you to fill in) or when a required environment variable is not set. Fill it in with amie packages setup x.jar, or amie packages config x.jar key=value, and open it again. A package that declares nothing runs as before, and its panel's REQUIREMENTS shows the same verdict Package x.jar not found: not in the env, AMP/pluginDir, as a path, or in the GitHub repositories of AMP/github.json The jar is nowhere local and no repository of AMP/github.json has it; check packages.available() and the token for a private repository x.jar has no package class: a public class with run(String): List and close(), and a no-arg constructor The jar does not follow the package contract, see Packages Script is already running Wait for Finished or Failed; sessions are unaffected Many name.jar #n rows under Sessions Package sessions are one per initMod call; close them in the script or press Terminate all

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Route settings, opened from the gears icon at the foot of the sidebar, and from everything that asks a guest to sign in; the window header has no account. The page scrolls, with the file tree in a box of its own at the foot. As in VS Code's settings, each part is a title over a card of rows: a setting's name and a line about it at the left, its control at the right, the rows divided by a thin rule. The controls are the app's own buttons and toggles.

docs.title: Account
docs.text: The first section, because it is where signing in lives (see Signing in). Signed out it says what signing in gives, with Sign in and Create account, which open the login and register pages; those come back here. Signed in it says who you are, with Log out, which ends the session here and at Keycloak. After a restart it shows you as signed in as soon as it opens, whatever Keycloak takes to answer. The backup under it is only available signed in, and says so otherwise.

docs.title: Backup
docs.text:
A guest sees that it needs an account, with Sign in to back up, and no button that does nothing.

Back up now stores your own work on the Amie backend under your account, in place of the last backup. It is one saved state named amp-backup, holding exactly these files and nothing else:

  • the scripts in AMP/templates: each <id>.kts with the <id>.json that describes it
  • AMP/settings.json
  • AMP/pluginDir/main.kts

This is an allowlist (settings/AccountBackup.kt). session.json, keycloak.json, databases.json, github.json, a model's serving.json with its key, models, logs, jars and anything else in the folder are never sent, and a link in the folder is not followed. The one thing it can't tell is what you wrote: a password typed into a script goes with the script.

The line under it says when the last backup was made and how many files it holds. The time comes from the backup on the backend, so it is right on another machine, and it reads Last backup unknown, with the reason, when the backend can't be reached.

The backend keeps a saved state of at most 1 MiB, measured on the JSON text it receives. A backup over that is refused whole, naming its size and the largest files, and nothing is sent, so the last backup stays as it was. It is never cut down to fit. A file that isn't UTF-8 text refuses the backup the same way, since it couldn't come back as it is.

Restore asks first, in a question under the backup (the same box every confirmation uses), and Keep my files changes nothing. It writes the backup's files back and deletes nothing, so a template the backup doesn't have stays. A file that would change is first copied to AMP/pluginDir/backup/<name>-<yyyyMMdd-HHmmss>.<ext>, as the editor keeps a script it replaces, so a replaced script shows under Previous scripts in the sandbox's Templates pane. The message afterwards names each file replaced and its copy. Settings restored apply at once, and a restored main.kts is in the editor the next time you open the sandbox. A backup that names any file off the allowlist writes nothing at all.

docs.title: Cloud save
docs.text: Logged in, what you save in the sandbox is also kept in your account, and logging in on another Mac brings it down. It uses the same three kinds of file as the backup and is described under Cloud save in the sandbox page; the backup above stays a separate, manual snapshot.

docs.title: The rest of the page
docs.text:
UI scale (under Appearance): how large everything is drawn. The presets (80, 90, 100, 110, 125, 150%) apply at once; the slider (70 to 150% in steps of 5) applies when it is let go. It is kept in AMP/settings.json with the sidebar choices of the sandbox and the Models page and whether the Models tab's first steps were dismissed.

Editor: the sandbox editor's text size, presets of 12, 13, 14, 15, 16 and 18pt (14 the default), its lines spaced to match; kept as editorFontSize. ⌥⌘+ / ⌥⌘− (Ctrl+Alt elsewhere) inside the editor change it by a point (11 to 20) and ⌘0 sets it back. re-indent on Enter (on by default, kept as reindentOnEnter): Enter re-indents the whole script as it starts the new line (Sandbox); off, Enter only starts the line at its depth, and ⌘⇧F still re-indents. Run details under Console (off by default, kept as runDetails): the run's status (Running 3s, Finished in 0s) and the figures of what it used, over the console, or over the editor while the console is hidden. Off, the console strip has only its level toggles, Find, Details and Clear, and the console only what the script logs. The line under it says where the script templates are kept.

The sidebar is the same as on every page, so Sandbox and Models are one click away; the back arrow in the window's top bar returns to the page Settings was opened from. The bar also has the page's sections as tabs (Account, Backup, Appearance, Editor, Models page, Files, those that show): a tab scrolls to its section, and the one selected is the section scrolled to. A row is its name and its control, the rest in its tooltip.

Models page: first steps shows the four first steps over the Models tab again after their Dismiss hid them (kept as firstStepsHidden); they show while one of them is undone (see Models page).

Model folders: every model's folder in one list (intent, text, speech and imported models, by kind), each row its name, kind and full path, with Copy path and Reveal. A model's own page no longer shows its path.

Files: the AMP folder as a tree, everything the app writes (models/, pluginDir/, env/, the json files). Every folder opens and closes, every file shows its size, Refresh reads it again and Reveal opens it in the file browser. A file or folder is deleted from its row (Delete, then the question that opens under the row, with Keep and a red Delete; a folder goes with everything in it). A folder left empty deletes itself: after a delete the folders left holding nothing go, and every read of the tree prunes the empty ones, since the app makes any folder it needs again. The root stays.

docs.title: Set up Amie on a new Mac
docs.text: From nothing to talking to Amie, in about 20 minutes, most of it downloads. These are the steps a fresh download was taken through on 3 November 2026: two clones, one setup script, one Gradle run.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• A Mac (Apple Silicon was tested) with about 8 GB free: 4 GB of models, the rest for Gradle and the build.
  • git, and access to the private samging/amieAppStable and samging/jar-jar repositories. gh auth login followed by gh auth setup-git is the quickest way.
  • Nothing else. Gradle downloads a JDK 21 when there is none. Amie is a desktop app on its own: there is no account to make and nothing to sign in to.

docs.title: 1. Clone both repositories side by side
docs.text:
mkdir -p ~/amie && cd ~/amie
git clone https://github.com/samging/amieAppStable.git
git clone https://github.com/samging/jar-jar.git

setup.sh takes the package jars (face, speech, microphone, mail, browser, mac, memory, files, spotify) from the jar-jar folder next to the app's. Until amieAppStable#1 and jar-jar#1 are merged, add -b app-update and -b jars-update to the two clones. Without them you get the older app and jars.

docs.title: 2. Download the models
docs.text:
~/amie/amieAppStable/AMP/setup/setup.sh

It took 11 minutes and wrote 3.9 GB to ~/Library/Application Support/amie pilot/AMP:

What Size For Llama 3.2 3B 2.6 GB Chat, and deciding what you meant when the intent model isn't sure BERT NER and the bge encoder 830 MB The intent model, which setup.sh puts in AMP/models/bert

Everything goes under AMP/models/: bert/, text/ (Llama), speech/ (Whisper and the voice), and intents/ once the talk has trained its model. An older install, with textModels/, modules/ and the speech models under pluginDir/config/speech/, is moved there by the app when it next starts; setup.sh skips what is already in either place. | Whisper small.en | 358 MB | Hearing you | | Supertonic 3 | 139 MB | Amie's voice |

It also copies the jars, the voice scripts, voice-actions.csv and the Talk to Amie template. Run it again whenever you like: it resumes downloads and skips what is there. AMIE_QWEN=1 also downloads Qwen 2.5 1.5B, for quicker, simpler answers.

docs.title: 3. Start the app
docs.text:
cd ~/amie/amieAppStable && ./gradlew :desktopApp:run

The first build downloads Gradle's dependencies and takes a few minutes. The app opens on the Sandbox.

docs.title: 4. Talk
docs.text:
1. Open Templates, pick Talk to Amie, and choose Load.
  2. Press Run. The first run trains the intent model from voice-actions.csv, which takes about half a minute.
  3. Type talk in the console and press Return. The face appears over your windows and says hello.
  4. Speak when the face listens. Say "goodbye" to end.

docs.title: The permissions macOS asks for
docs.text:
macOS asks before an app may listen or control other apps; Linux and Windows don't, and Amie asks nothing there.

When macOS asks If you said no The talk starts To let the terminal that started Gradle (or the Amie app, once packaged) use the microphone Amie says it can't hear you and opens System Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone. Turn it on and start the talk again Amie first uses Mail, Calendar, Reminders, Notes, Music or Spotify To let it control that app, once per app That action answers with an error. Turn it on under Privacy & Security > Automation

Without microphone access macOS gives an app silence rather than an error, so the talk checks first instead of listening to nothing.

Things to try, all of which worked on the fresh download:

Say Amie "Hello Amie, how are you today?" Answers through Llama "Remember that I like green tea" Saves it to AMP/pluginDir/config/memory/memories.txt "How is my battery?" "Battery is at 69%, charging." "What song is this?" Names what Spotify plays "Goodbye" "Talk soon!"

The full list is in Talk to Amie.

docs.title: Optional
docs.text:
• Spotify by name. "Play Drake" opens a search unless Spotify keys are set. Make an app at developer.spotify.com, then put clientId= and clientSecret= in AMP/pluginDir/config/spotify/spotify.properties. Pause, next and "what song is this" need no keys.
  • Mail. Add your accounts to the Mail app first. Amie only sends a mail after you say yes to the draft.
  • Start talking at launch. AMIE_AUTORUN=1 ./gradlew :desktopApp:run runs the loaded main.kts as soon as the app opens.
  • Accounts. Signing in, backups, cloud save and the package repository are off in this desktop version. AMIE_ACCOUNTS=1 turns them back on, with Keycloak and the Amie backend running (Keycloak setup).
  • Another data folder. AMIE_AMP_DIR=<folder> for both setup.sh and the app keeps a second, separate Amie.
  • A Mac app with the models inside. Run ./gradlew :desktopApp:packageDistributionForCurrentOS -Pamie.modelsDir="$HOME/Library/Application Support/amie pilot/AMP/models/bert".

docs.title: When something goes wrong
docs.text:
You see Do No space left on device Free a few GB. Downloads resume when you run setup.sh again No BERT models at ... Run setup.sh again, or set AMIE_MODELS_DIR to a folder with model.onnx and bge/model.onnx A jar is missing, or old Make sure jar-jar sits next to amieAppStable, on the branch from step 1, and run setup.sh again "I can't hear you yet" Allow the microphone for your terminal under Privacy & Security > Microphone, then restart the app Property logger is not found in the bindings Fixed in a0133dc: pull. Until then, start with JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS=-Damie.prewarm=false

More in Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Where the code is
docs.text:
The app's Kotlin is under amieApplication/desktopApp/src/main/kotlin/org/example/project/, the tests in src/test/kotlin/ under the same folders. Most of it is in components/terminal/window/controller/, whose folders say what a file is:

Folder What is in it (the folder itself) The window: TerminalWindow (and LogLevel), ToolWindows, CommandPalette, ConfigurationPanel, ConnectionPanel models/ The Models page (ModelsPage the layout, ModelsPageState its state and actions, ModelsGuide the guide tab) and what it shows of one model: list, snapshot, detail, tabs, Try, Improve, decisions, new model tabs/ The other tabs of that page: groups, packages and their repository, sessions amp/ The layout of the models in the AMP folder, ModelFolders (the one owner of models/bert, models/intents, models/text, models/speech), and their move into it at start, ModelsMigration pages/ What the pages share: ManageablePage, PageKeys, notices, polling; the shared pieces of a page (Hint, Fold, SearchField, DetailPanel, …) are in components/ui/viewport/, see The components console/ The console: lines and colors, find in it, the sessions it ends, what is running now and what it uses, the memory watch sandbox/ The sandbox page: CodingSandbox (the layout), SandboxStrips (the editor header and the console strip), SandboxRunStatus (the run's dot, figures and outcome), SandboxFolds (Recent runs, Still open, Kept away), the editor with its folding and formatting, the templates pane, the examples, the export panel, the run history script/ What runs a script: ScriptRuntime (assembleScript, ScriptRunner), ScriptLogger, SandboxLogger, SandboxApi (the API a script calls), templates, errors, MainScriptRun, background templates, shell commands modules/ The AMP modules a script names by import: AmpModules (readModule, updateModule, ...), ModuleMetrics, ModelVersions, ModelGroups, ModelJobs, OrtScopes, SharedModels runtime/ A model at work: the HTTP server, sessions, text and speech models, the session log and run records, run resources metrics/ What is said of a model: metrics charts and images, score intervals, validation, requirements, the model card util/ Small helpers: file sizes, local times, version compare, stamped reads, system stats, the desktop (file chooser, browser), number formats jetbrainDLBuilder/, modelLoaders/, envBuilder/, export/, pluginEngine/, sourceFile/, databases/ Building models, loading them, the script environment, the compiled bundles, jar packages, data sources, databases

A file's package is its folder, and a test is in the same folder as the file it tests.

docs.title: What must stay where it is
docs.text: Saved scripts, the templates under AMP/templates and the code the sandbox generates name some classes by their full name: LogLevel (in TerminalWindow.kt), the functions and types of modules/ and the packages jetbrainDLBuilder, sourceFile, envBuilder and databases. Moving those would break a saved main.kts, so they stay in their packages. SandboxApi and CompiledRuntime (in export/) spell the other class names out, so they follow a moved class.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
desktopApp/build.gradle.kts sorts the tests into suites by package: testModels takes jetbrainDLBuilder, modules, runtime, metrics, util, modelLoaders and integrations; testScripts takes the rest of controller; testUi, testPerf and testApp take ui, perf and bench, and what is left of org.example.project. A new folder under controller/ is in testScripts unless it is added to testModels.

A test file is named after the source file it tests, <Name>Test.kt or <Name><Aspect>Test.kt, so that ./test.sh file <Name> finds it, and holds the tests of that one file or feature. What tests share lives in org.example.project.support: RecordingLogger and runScriptLines (main.kts run on the real engine, every line it logs kept), NoGithubRepos and withNoGithubRepos (AMP/github.json listing no repositories while a page is open, so it stays off the network), fakeKeycloak (a mock engine answering as Keycloak does), onAnyThread (Dispatchers.Main on the test's thread). The page tests drive a page by its texts with ui/PageDriving.kt (click, await, settle, type, press); the training tests build models with jetbrainDLBuilder/TrainingFixtures.kt (FakeEmbedder, rows, writeCsv); the page harness (ui/PageHarness.kt) is the real page off-screen with screenshots, extended by PageShotsTest and CodingSandboxTourTest. A fixture a few tests of one folder share stays in that folder, as BackgroundRunFixture, PackageJarFixture and BackgroundTemplatesFixture do.

docs.title: Sign-in
docs.text:
I am signed out every time the app starts. Before 2026-10-14 the app only had Keycloak's normal refresh token, which the realm expires after 30 minutes without use, and a Keycloak that was not reachable at start also deleted the session. Now every sign-in asks for an offline token, and a Keycloak that is unreachable or answers with an error of its own keeps the session. If Account in Settings still shows you signed out: check AMP/logs.txt for lines starting with auth:. "Keycloak refused the saved session" means the realm revoked it (sign in again); "couldn't refresh … kept, will retry" means Keycloak is down, see below.

"Couldn't renew your session, Keycloak isn't answering". You are still signed in; the access token expired and Keycloak can't renew it right now. Start Keycloak and try again; there is no need to sign in.

"Keycloak is not reachable" on the login page. Run docker ps. The Keycloak container restarts in a loop while its Postgres container is down:

docker start my-ubuntu-image-postgresql-1
docker start my-ubuntu-image-keycloak-1
curl -s http://localhost:8080/realms/master/.well-known/openid-configuration | head -c 100

"Wrong username or password" with the right password. Use the username; the realm does not log in by email.

"Client 'amie' rejected". The client is confidential: put its secret in AMP/keycloak.json or KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_SECRET.

The browser sign-in hangs. The realm's frontend URL points at an old LAN address. Fix it under Realm settings → General in the admin console (see Keycloak setup).

Port in use when signing in with the browser. Change redirectPort in AMP/keycloak.json and add http://localhost:<port>/* to the client's redirect URIs.

docs.title: Sandbox
docs.text:
import("…") without the prefix does not compile. Kotlin reads it as an import statement. Use implementation("group:module:version"), dependency("…"), environment(SettingsEnv(…)) or amie.import("…").

"env '' must be selected with a literal environment(SettingsEnv("", ...)) or amie.import(SettingsEnv(...)) to be sourced". The environment call must be written literally in the script (environment(SettingsEnv("name", "profile")) or amie.import(SettingsEnv(...))); it is read from the text before the script compiles.

modelBuilder fails to embed. The encoder folder is missing; see Getting started.

metricsChart says there are no metrics. The model was never built in this AMP/, or its name differs from the folder under AMP/models/intents/.

docs.title: Models page and backend
docs.text:
"The backend rejected the Keycloak token (401)". The backend was started without the Keycloak verifier settings, or its KEYCLOAK_ISSUER does not match the realm's frontend URL. See Amie backend.

"Connection refused: ensure the Amie backend is running". Nothing listens at the address in AMP/backend.json. With Keycloak on 8080, run the backend with AMIE_BACKEND_PORT=8090: the app moves a baseUrl on 8080 to 8090 by itself (and saves it) when 8090 answers; set it by hand only when the backend is somewhere else.

Publish reads Publish (sign in). You are a guest; pressing it opens Account in Settings, where you sign in. Publishing uploads under your account, so it needs a Keycloak sign-in; the metrics and statistics on the page do not.

docs.title: Performance tests
docs.text:
desktopApp/src/test/kotlin/org/example/project/perf/ measures the app and asserts each figure under a budget about three times what it measured on the Mac it was written on; the budget and that measurement stand beside each other in the test. Every figure is printed as perf <name>: <value> (budget …), so a run on a slower machine says what it got. The tests that open a model use the real bge encoder with AMIE_E2E_ENCODER=1 (seconds to load, hundreds of MB outside the heap) and a stand-in model without it, so the figures are of the app around the model either way.

cd amieApplication
./gradlew :desktopApp:test --tests 'org.example.project.perf.*' --no-configuration-cache --rerun
AMIE_E2E_ENCODER=1 ./gradlew :desktopApp:test --tests 'org.example.project.perf.*' --no-configuration-cache --rerun
Test What is measured Budget StartupPerfTest main's root composed off screen: the first frame, and the sandbox on screen after the start route sends on 4 s, 12 s BundledModels.root and SharedEncoders when first touched; with the encoder, its first load, a second acquire, the last release 50 ms each; 10 s, 50 ms, 2 s ModelsPagePerfTest readSnapshot(remote = false), what the page reads every 1.5 s, with 1, 20 and 60 models in AMP/models/intents; it may grow linearly in the count and no worse 150 ms, 400 ms, 1 s; 60 at most 3.5× what 20 added The Models page composed on an empty cache with 60 models: its first frame, the first model on screen 5 s, 8 s MemoryPerfTest A session opened, asked and closed 20 times: heap drift after System.gc(), the encoder's holder count back where it was, no ORT session left 24 MB Two models on one encoder folder load it once: the second open costs its head only first 10 s, second 1 s sharedModel("dummy") taken ten times: one snapshot with ten holders, freed by the last close, the heap and the encoder back 24 MB drift Eight background template runs at once: started, all ready on their own engines, the heap they hold, the ninth refused, what stays once they end 2 s, 45 s, 900 MB or 85 % of the heap, 150 MB Terminate all in the page's order: no model session, shared model, package, ORT session or run left, no encoder loaded 3 s WindowsPerfTest Sandbox → Models → the model's detail panel → back → Settings → back, ten rounds through the real sidebar and header: no exception in the log, threads not climbing after the second round, at most the status strip's own two or three SystemStats.read() calls in five seconds once the Models page is away first round 15 s, median 9 s, 6 threads, 4 reads The whole window opened and closed ten times (each start composes the Devices dashboard on its way to the sandbox); no read of the process once they are closed first 12 s, median 5 s, 6 threads, 1 read PopupsPerfTest The command palette (a popup of its own over 300 entries) opened and closed 40 times: no popup left, its hold on the page's keys given back each time, no thread; a query over 5000 entries first 10 s, median 3 s, 6 threads; 1 s ConsolePerfTest A script printing 40000 lines from a thread of its own: the console stays between 18000 and 20000 lines with the newest, logs.txt has all of them, the heap is back after clearing produce 20 s, drain 30 s, 40 MB Eight threads of 2000 lines: every line in the file and the console, each thread's in order; 15 megabyte lines pass 20 MB and logs.txt moves to logs.1.txt; clearConsole over 10000 lines 20 s; 30 s; 500 ms ConsoleCapViewPerfTest A full console shown and followed takes 3000 more lines in thirty batches of 100: the oldest 2000 go at once when the cap is passed (one by one, every batch composed all 20000 lines again: 1.2 s a batch), the view stays at the newest compose 40 s, mean batch at the cap 600 ms ConsoleCommandsPerfTest scopes, clear, the aliases (open, still, close, ?) in any case, terminate by name closing every session of that name; 300 commands in a row answered with no thread left; terminate all over ten models, a bare ORT session and three background templates 20 s, 6 threads; 5 s RunResourcesPerfTest The Resources line of a run that burns CPU and opens and closes a session: memory within the machine's RAM, peak at least the end, heap within its limit, CPU between a quarter of the burn and every core, one session opened and closed; a run that holds 192 MB says at least 48 MB more and a heap of 60 MB the machine's own limits RunMeterPerfTest A run that sleeps two seconds: the CPU the meter's own thread spends on its three readings (the ps child's own CPU is outside the JVM) 1 % of a core 30 runs started and stopped: no amie-run-meter thread left 6 s

A figure over budget fails the test with the line it printed. On a machine slower than the budgets allow, the printed figures say by how much; the budgets are in the tests, next to the measurement they were taken from.

docs.title: Slow hardware
docs.text:
To see what the app costs on a machine, start it with --bench (on a Pi: ./scripts/pi-bench.sh); Raspberry Pi 5 has what it measures and what it found.

The app runs on a Raspberry Pi (4 GB, four cores, an SD card) and on older Macs with 8 GB. What costs most there is the encoder: bge is 800 MB on disk and about 1.2 GB once ONNX Runtime has loaded it, outside the Java heap, and it is loaded once and shared by every session, listener, validation and build on it.

What to set. The heap may grow to 35% of the machine's RAM (-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=35 in the build: 1.4 GB on a 4 GB Pi, 2.8 GB with 8 GB). To change that for one machine, set AMIE_JVM_ARGS where the app is built or run, as in AMIE_JVM_ARGS="-Xmx2g" ./gradlew :desktopApp:run; a DEB or MSI built with the variable set carries the flags in its launcher.

  • An 8 GB Mac: the defaults, or AMIE_JVM_ARGS="-Xmx2g" when the machine swaps with the app open. That leaves the encoder, the system and a browser room.
  • A 4 GB Raspberry Pi: AMIE_JVM_ARGS="-Xmx1g -XX:+UseSerialGC -Damie.ort.threads=3". One gigabyte of heap is enough for the page, scripts and a build of some thousand rows; the serial collector keeps the JVM's own threads off the four cores; three ONNX threads leave one core for the window. An 8 GB Pi takes -Xmx2g and the default threads.
  • -Damie.timing=true prints, on standard output, when the window was composed and when the Models page had its first read, counted from the JVM's start, so a slow start can be placed.
  • -Damie.ort.threads=N sets how many threads each ONNX session gets (one per core by default), and -Damie.ort.default=true opens sessions with ONNX Runtime's own options, to compare.

What the app does on its own. The threads of an ONNX session sleep when the session is idle instead of spinning for more work, so an encoder, a few heads and a group open at once don't take the cores between requests (an idle encoder went from 8 ms to 2 ms of CPU in two seconds on a Mac). A build runs the rows through the encoder 32 at a time, each batch rows of the same number of tokens, which gives the very vectors one row at a time gives about five times quicker (2 ms a row instead of 11 on a Mac). It keeps only each row's sentence vector (3 KB), not its whole hidden state (about 200 KB), so ten thousand rows take 30 MB of heap where they took 2 GB. The Models page reads the models again every 1.5 seconds and the status strip every 2, and when a read takes long on a slow disk the next one waits three times as long; a model's metrics history is decoded once and kept until its file changes; the process's memory is read from /proc on Linux and from one ps a second at most elsewhere. The plots of the models are drawn on a thread of their own, at the lowest priority, and shown as they are ready, where the page's first read used to draw every one before showing anything (1.3 of its 1.9 seconds with twelve models on a Mac); the plots that follow a serving model's log are drawn again at most every ten seconds instead of after every answer. Background templates run at most eight at a time on a heap of 512 MB or more and fewer on a smaller one (one per 64 MB), each holding a Kotlin script engine of its own, measured at 32 to 49 MB.

When memory is short. The status strip at the foot of the window turns red when the process holds over 85% of the RAM or the heap is over 90% full: close the sessions and stop the listeners you don't need (a listener keeps its encoder; Terminate all closes sessions and templates but not listeners, which load the encoder again on their next request). An encoder that would not load leaves a line in the console starting encoder: couldn't load, with what the process held and what the machine had free. An out of memory error nobody caught leaves a line starting Out of memory on thread, with the heap limit it ran into; the app goes on, and what that thread was doing (a build, a page's read) is lost and can be started again. A template that can't start because the cap is reached says so with the heap it was counted against.

docs.title: Talk to Amie
docs.text: Speak, and Amie does what you said or answers out loud. ./scripts/setup.sh puts everything in place once: about 4 GB of free ONNX models, the shell scripts and the template. Then Templates > Talk to Amie > Load, and Run. The script loads nothing until you type talk in the console.

docs.title: A companion on your Mac
docs.text:
Amie has a face, greets you, remembers what you ask it to, and works the Mac through small jars with no keys. face.jar floats over your windows: it listens, thinks, talks and smiles along with the talk, and you can drag it anywhere. Close the app while it talks and it keeps going; the menu bar's face brings the window back or quits.

Say What happens "Any new email?", "Read the second email" mail.jar reads the Mail app. Add your accounts there first "Reply to the first email and say I'll be there" Llama writes it, it opens as a draft in Mail, and Amie reads it out and asks. Only a yes sends it; anything else leaves the draft "Write an email to Anna saying I'm late" The same draft and question, to the address of Anna's last mail in your inbox "Search the web for pizza near me" browser.jar, as a search in the browser "Play Daft Punk", "Next song", "What song is this" spotify.jar "Make a note to buy coffee", "Set a timer for five minutes" mac.jar, on Music or Spotify (mac.properties) and Notes. A timer lasts while the talk does "Open YouTube", "Open the browser" browser.jar, in your default browser or the one set in browser.properties "Open Notes", "Quit Spotify", "Set the volume to 30", "How's my battery?" mac.jar "What's on my calendar today?", "Remind me to call mum" mac.jar, on Calendar and Reminders "Open man.webp", "Create a new file main.py", "Read notes.txt", "Find my resume" files.jar, which finds by name in your home folder and never deletes or overwrites "What's on my calendar tomorrow?", "Put a haircut on my calendar on Friday at 3 pm" mac.jar "Who wrote War and Peace?", "What's happening in Poland?" browser.jar reads Wikipedia and the news, and Llama answers from that alone "Any mail from the bank?" mail.jar searches your inbox "Turn it up", "Dark mode", "Take a screenshot", "How much space is left?" mac.jar "Close this tab", "What are my newest files?" browser.jar and files.jar "Goodbye" Ends the talk. If you stay quiet, the face falls asleep and wakes when you speak "Remember that I like green tea" memory.jar, one line each in AMP/pluginDir/config/memory/memories.txt "Catch me up" mail, calendar and battery together

Amie hears you out: microphone.jar records until you stop talking, up to 20 seconds. When the intent model is at least 98.5% sure it acts at once, which takes no time. Otherwise Llama reads your words and picks what to do, which takes a few seconds, and anything that makes no sense gets "Sorry, I didn't catch that" instead of an action. To teach it how you talk, add rows to voice-actions.csv, delete AMP/models/intents/amie-intents, and it trains again. To answer faster and hear a little less, set whisper=whisper-base.en in the Packages tab.

The first use of each app makes macOS ask to let Amie control it, under System Settings > Privacy & Security > Automation. Mail and the calendar are read out as they are: only a chat or a catch-up goes through Llama, and text in an email can't trigger an action.

docs.title: What happens to what you say
docs.text:
1. microphone.jar records five seconds, and Whisper turns them into text.
  2. The amie-intents BERT intent model picks an action. It trains itself from AMP/voice-actions.csv on the first Run. Under a score of 0.5 the words count as a question.
  3. The action runs: a script of AMP/pluginDir/voice, or Llama.
  4. The Supertonic voice speaks, and microphone.jar plays it.

When the next turn starts, the console says where the last one's time went, from Whisper on, without the wait for you to speak: Took … ms: hearing … ms, intent … ms, Llama … ms, voice … ms, playing … ms. A part that didn't run that turn isn't listed, and Llama counts every question it was asked.

Action For example What it does weather "What's the weather in London?" weather.sh, from wttr.in list_files "List the files in my downloads" list-files.sh find_file "Find the file called notes" find-file.sh, by Spotlight on a Mac web_search "Who wrote Hamlet?" web-search.sh, from DuckDuckGo, then Llama open_terminal "Open a terminal in downloads" open-terminal.sh close_terminals "Close all terminals" close-terminals.sh, only when the model is at least 0.9 sure; what runs in them ends too edit_file "Edit the file called notes" edit-file.sh, in the default text editor open_vim "Open the readme in vim" open-vim.sh, in a new Terminal window brew_install "Brew install ripgrep" brew-install.sh, only when the model is at least 0.9 sure, and only a formula name chat "Tell me a joke" Llama

To teach it another action, add rows to the CSV, delete AMP/models/intents/amie-intents, and add a branch to the when of the script.

docs.title: What Amie manages
docs.text:
Llama, the intent model, Whisper, the voice and microphone.jar are sessions of the app: they are in Still open, under their own names, and Stop or Terminate ends them. initMod("whisper") and initMod("voice") open the ones speech.properties names, and a block such as ortClosable holds them like any model. Each loads when first used and stays until talking ends. Their memory is native, so the session shows what they weigh on disk.

Which Whisper, which voice, how fast it talks and how many threads it uses are in speech.properties, and the microphone in microphone.properties. speaker picks who talks: 0 af, 1 af_bella, 2 af_nicole, 3 af_sarah, 4 af_sky, 5 am_adam, 6 am_michael, 7 bf_emma, 8 bf_isabella, 9 bm_george, 10 bm_lewis. Any Piper voice of sherpa-onnx also works if you put it beside them and name it in voice. Both open in the Packages tab. The models sit beside that file, in AMP/models/speech.

docs.title: When a command fails
docs.text:
Each command goes through .patchBy(::explain). A command that fails hands what it said to explain, which asks Llama why and speaks the answer. patchBy takes any function, so the same error can go elsewhere:

shellScript("voice/brew-install.sh", listOf("wget"))
    .patchBy(::log)                                  // the console
    .patchBy { error -> speak(error) }               // the voice, word for word
    .patchBy { error -> log(llama.answer(error)) }   // a model
    .patchBy(::handleBy)                             // the local text model, with main.kts and the env in view

What a failed command printed is in the error terminal too, with why it failed: errorLog() pulls its last lines, and handleBy() hands them to the local text model, so a script can ask about the whole of what the console showed in red, not only the one command.

textModel in the script picks the model: llama3.2-3b (about 3 GB of memory) or the faster qwen2.5-1.5b (about 1.3 GB). Other exports go in AMP/models/text. An export that needs a graphics card won't load here.

docs.title: In an exported bundle
docs.text: Export the template as any script. The intent model, the text model, the two packages, the speech models and the shell scripts all go along, and talk is read from standard input. speech.jar carries the native library of Apple silicon only, so the bundle runs on those Macs.

docs.title: 1.1.0: encoders and decoders, projects, and the templates' three verbs
docs.text:
• Encoder and decoder pairs. A sequence-to-sequence export (T5, BART, Marian translation, Whisper) is two ONNX files, encoder_model.onnx with decoder_model.onnx, which no single run answers. amie hf import now takes the pair whole: it lists every encoder and decoder of the folder, the full variant marked, to pick with the arrow keys (space takes or leaves the file under the cursor, Enter imports, n leaves; --take names them for a pipe or a script), with the config, tokenizer and preprocessor files alongside. Any repo with several files that run here is picked the same way, the file hf info says an import takes already marked. hf info marks the pair's files. initMod("<name>") opens both sessions as .encoder and .decoder (.decoderWithPast when exported), with .tokens(text), .text(ids), .startToken and .endToken from the files beside them. See Encoder and decoder pairs.
  • The encoder's input made for you. m.encode(text) runs the tokenizer and the encoder; m.encode(file) reads the model's preprocessor_config.json and turns a wav or aiff into Whisper's log-mel spectrogram, or an image into normalized pixels, then runs the encoder. m.decoderFeeds(encoded, ids) fills the decoder's inputs by name, and m.startTokens(encoded, "de", "translate") gives the decoder's first ids from the config's forced tokens, each replaceable by a name the config knows, Whisper's language detected when none is given. A script's own part is the twelve-line greedy loop. Whisper tiny transcribes a spoken wav exactly, and a quantized T5 translates.
  • amie models remove <name>. Removes a model's folder whatever its kind, an intent, text, speech or imported model, closing a session of it first. Paths are printed as a shell takes them, Application\ Support.
  • amie models info on an imported model lists its files by role (the encoder, the decoders, or the model and the files beside it), the config and tokenizer files with their sizes, the start and end tokens, its labels, and how initMod opens it.
  • ortRequired in place of ortTimed. ortRequired("name") { } keeps what its block opens while anything else is in session, a model, package, group, template or background job, and frees it within a couple of seconds once nothing else is open; its block opens it again when next run, as lazily as ortStatic. For what other models need beside them. ortTimed is gone from scripts: a saved script that calls it no longer compiles. The starter Scope functions is brought up to date in every AMP folder where it was never saved over.
  • Help that reads. amie <command> --help puts every action on its own line with its description wrapped beneath and a blank line between them, as wide as the terminal; :help wraps the same way.
  • Projects. amie new <name> makes AMP/projects/<name>/main.kts to start from, in an env of the same name; amie run <name> runs it.
  • Export without the jars. amie templates export <name> --out <folder> --no-jars leaves the env's Maven jars and the package jars out of the bundle and writes require.txt, one line a file with the path to put it at under the bundle; the README has the same table. run.jar --check says which are still missing. A run with a Maven jar missing fetches it from Maven Central when it can reach it, and with a package jar missing stops and names it. Compiled bundles from amie now carry the app's own classes: before this the runner was missing from run.jar.
  • Templates: save, edit, delete. amie templates save <name> <file> keeps a script file, a project or a starter as a template (a name taken is saved again, its id kept); amie templates edit <name> opens its file in $VISUAL or $EDITOR and takes the edit, or prints the path when neither is set; amie templates delete <name> removes it.
  • Piper voices import ready to speak. A Piper voice from the Hub (rhasspy/piper-voices, a path to one voice) lands in AMP/models/speech, laid out as sherpa-onnx wants it, its ONNX metadata added when the export lacks it. A path that names no voice is refused instead of another voice being taken in its place.
  • Installing on a machine without Java. install.sh finds a JDK 21 or installs one: Homebrew's on a Mac, apt's on Debian and Ubuntu, else a Temurin build from Adoptium into ~/.local/lib/jdk-21; --no-jdk leaves that out.
  • Fixes at the prompt. :help lists every command line of amie, each as amie <command> --help when it has more than one action, with no example line repeated. The line editor no longer expands !! as shell history, which broke Kotlin's non-null assertion in a pasted block. A name initMod can't find says every folder it looked in and names amie models list and amie hf import. A tokenizer with an empty "Precompiled" normalizer (Marian's) no longer aborts the process. amie models list wraps a model's labels instead of running off the row, and a pair shows none.

docs.title: Less said twice
docs.text:
• System usage on the Sessions tab. The line over the sessions says what the process holds of the machine's RAM and how much of that is the encoders, the heap, the native memory, the cpu, the threads and what the sessions weigh, and "near the limit" when it is. The memory strip at the foot of the window is gone, and so is Memory in the rail; the strip shows only while something runs.
  • TensorFlow on the Hub. The Hugging Face search for TensorFlow asks for the tf-keras tag, where the SavedModels are, as well as tf, whose repos are nearly all Keras .h5 weights that don't run here; an empty answer says so.
  • A package's manual. The package panel opens with Manual: the description of the jar's metadata, which says what the package does and the texts it answers, with its notes. Copy script beside Opens with puts a three-line script on the clipboard: open the package, call it with its first test's text, close it.
  • Paths only in Settings. The package panel's Where, Page, Download and File lines are gone, and so is the config folder's path; Settings has a Package folders group with every jar's path and config folder, Copy path, Reveal jar and Reveal config. The Model folders rows say the encoder's path; About names the encoder. A group's panel no longer says where groups.json is, and the New model form shows the chosen file's name.
  • Created moved to Settings. When a model was made is on its row under Settings, Model folders, with its kind and its folder; the About tab's Details no longer say it.
  • Three labels, and how many more. About's Labels line names the three labels with the most training rows, "chat, weather, list_files and 7 more"; the rows per label stay on the Data tab, which is also the only place that says what the preprocessor did to the rows.
  • Templates and Console in the header. The Sandbox's two toggles sit at the left of the header strip, before the + for a new template; the strip no longer names main.kts, and the Models page's New model is a + with the words in its tooltip.

docs.title: Hugging Face tasks, one New model, and two hues
docs.text:
• Every kind of model the Hub has. The Hugging Face search has a task menu beside its format chips: Text to speech, Speech recognition, Text classification, Token classification, Feature extraction, Text generation, Audio classification and Image classification, or Any task. A task alone lists the Hub's most downloaded models of it. A looked-up repo says its task, model type and the labels of its config.json before anything is downloaded, and the labels and the task are written into the imported model's source.json, shown on its row and panel, and found by the filter. A speech model's voices, tokens, lexicon and phoneme data, and a Piper voice's .onnx.json, come along with it. In a script, huggingFace.search("", task = "text-to-speech") (or tts, ner, embeddings…). See From Hugging Face.
  • One New model. The Models page's New model opens one form whose first line says where the model comes from, A csv or Hugging Face; the cloud chip is gone, and the list, the rule and the panel sit closer. See New model.
  • Blue and green. The app is no longer gray alone: a dark blue fills the one primary button of a place, a lighter blue draws links, the focus ring, a focused field, the open tab's bar, a selected row's edge and the line of a build or a download, and a faint blue washes what is selected; the muted green marks what runs, succeeded or is done, the bar of a notice included. Accents, never floods; every word keeps 4.5:1 and every mark 3:1 (ContrastTest). See Colour.

docs.title: The error terminal's lines go to handleBy
docs.text: • Pull the console's error lines, and hand them to handleBy. errorLog() is the error terminal's log: the last error lines the console showed, oldest first, a run's failures, what a command printed on stderr and why it failed, the app's own. handleBy() hands the last ten of them to the local text model with main.kts and the env, so after a failed command or run one call asks about what the console showed in red; handleBy(lines) takes any list, and shell("x").patchBy(::handleBy) asks about what the one command said the moment it fails. Clear, ⌘K and a new run empty it. See Scripting API.

docs.title: Models from Hugging Face
docs.text:
• Add from Hugging Face. The cloud chip after New model on the Models page searches the Hub, in every format initMod opens or one of them (ONNX, TorchScript, TensorFlow, TFLite), and also takes a repo id or a huggingface.co address. It lists the repo's runnable files by format with their sizes and says why the weights-only files won't run. It picks a plain model.onnx with its config and tokenizer files and downloads the pick into AMP/models/imported/<name>, with progress and Cancel. Leaving the page doesn't stop the download. The files only take their names once their sizes check, so a closed app never leaves a half file, and the next download resumes. See From Hugging Face.
  • Imported models are listed. They have their own fold, Imported, showing each model's format, source repo and size, with a Delete that asks first.
  • huggingFace("owner/name") in a script downloads the model the first time and returns its local name, so initMod(huggingFace("owner/name")) works; huggingFace.search("bert", format = "onnx") returns repo ids. A gated or private repo reads HF_TOKEN from the environment, and the token is never logged or stored. See Scripting API.
  • Model folders in one place. The full path of a model's folder is gone from its page (the About tab's block is Details now) and from an imported model's panel; Settings lists every model's folder in Model folders, by kind, with Copy path and Reveal
  • A language model answers in text. Logits like GPT-2's [1, 1, 50257] were shown as "hidden state [1, 1, 50257]"; they are a score for every token at every place, and an imported language model now decodes them: one that continues text gives the text it goes on with (greedy, up to 24 tokens) and its 5 likeliest next tokens, one that fills a mask the likeliest tokens at [MASK]

docs.title: PyTorch and TensorFlow models
docs.text:
• initMod opens models made elsewhere. initMod("<name>") opens AMP/models/imported/<name>, a Hugging Face repo or a folder copied in, and initMod("/path/model.pt") or the new importModel(path) a model by its path: ONNX on the bundled runtime, TorchScript (.pt, .pth, .torchscript) on PyTorch, a TensorFlow SavedModel folder on TensorFlow. A folder of several formats opens its ONNX, else the one its source.json names, else the first that runs here, and says which. See Models from outside.
  • Tensors in and out. A model from a file says what it takes and gives (.inputs, .outputs: name, shape, type) and runs on numbers: .run(floatArrayOf(…)), .run(longArrayOf(…)), .run(mapOf("input_ids" to ids)). Text still goes in when a tokenizer.json is next to it, and the labels come from its config.json. importModelOnnx models answer the same calls.
  • Natives on first use. PyTorch and TensorFlow come as DJL engines whose jars are small; their native libraries (about 40 MB for PyTorch on an Apple Silicon Mac, 130 to 150 MB for TensorFlow) are downloaded into ~/.djl.ai the first time one of their models is opened, which the console says once. Offline, the first open says what it wanted.
  • Refused, with what would work. TFLite (DJL has no TFLite engine since 0.28), frozen TensorFlow graphs, PyTorch weights saved with torch.save, and weights alone (safetensors, pytorch_model.bin, gguf, h5) are refused, naming every file and the way to ONNX or TorchScript. PyTorch has no natives for Intel Macs, and TensorFlow 2 is in the lightweight build only, since the full build's TensorFlow 1.15 clashes with it.
  • Listed and closed like the others. Each one is a row of the Sessions tab with Terminate, closed with the ortClosable block around it, and hasModel("name") is true for an imported model. importModelTensorflow is importModel now, and the old TensorFlow 1.15 and TFLite loaders, which did nothing, are gone.
  • An Apple Silicon Mac builds the lightweight app. TensorFlow 1.15 has no natives for it, and its classes kept TensorFlow 2 out, so a Mac like that now builds without it, as a Raspberry Pi does: about 700 MB less, and initMod opens TensorFlow SavedModels there. -Pamie.lightweight=false builds the full one

docs.title: Quicker builds, where a turn's time goes, and setup in AMP/setup
docs.text:
• The editor marks wrong calls as you type. A moment after typing stops, a call to the script API with too few or too many arguments, a named argument the function hasn't, a literal of the wrong type (initMod(12)) or an unknown member (amie.lgo("x")) gets a red wavy line and a dot by its line number; the pointer on it says what is wrong. See The editor.
  • handleBy("error") asks the local text model, and the AI pane is gone. handleBy("Unresolved reference: dumy") (or handleBy(e) for what was thrown, as in handleBy({ e -> handleBy(e) }) { … }) asks a text model of AMP/models/text what is wrong and how to fix it, with main.kts and the env in its prompt, prints the answer and returns it. It only answers: the script stays as it is. The sparkle on the rail, ⌘2 and the pane that wrote whole scripts went, as a small model's whole scripts were often wrong
  • The console remembers. The lines of script typed at >>> share one interpreter: val x = 12, then log(x) prints 12, and a fun, class or import stays for the next line. A line that ends in a value prints it. A block can go over several lines: for (x in 0..10) waits at a ... prompt until {, log(x) and } make it whole, then runs once. A blank line sends a block whose brackets are closed, Ctrl+C drops it (or stops a line that runs), and reset forgets the definitions. Lines run in the order they were typed.
  • shell prints at the internal level. shell("ls -l") shows the command and what it prints as internal lines, its stderr as errors, so a script's own info lines aren't buried under a listing. Turn Internal on to see them; .out, .lines and .err keep everything.
  • The editor's list offers each name once. info, log, error, data, output, import, initMod, sessionMod and the rest with overloads were listed once per overload (info(message: String) and info(message: Any?)); each is one row now, the form a script writes most: initMod(""), info(""), import("").
  • The sandbox's bar reads as IntelliJ's. The env is a flat run-configuration widget (a small box, its name, a chevron), and Run, Stop and export are thin outlined icons, a green triangle, a red square and an arrow, all of one size.
  • Gray, not blue, as IntelliJ's dark chrome. Every background, border and text gray is neutral now (the editor #0E0E0E, the panels and bars #151515, the borders #242424, the text #BFBFBF), at the same steps of lightness, so every word still reaches 4.5:1. The primary button (New model, Open session, Validate, Build) is filled light gray with dark words in place of blue, and while disabled is a plain gray chip. A selected model is a gray step with a brighter edge, the chosen completion a gray step, the open tab's underline and the keyboard's focus ring are light gray, the editor's selection is a gray band as the IDE's inactive selection, and the Metrics charts and the confusion matrix are grays told apart by lightness and by each series' mark. Text selected in any field is the same gray. The code's colours are as they were, and the flags named slate and blue keep their hues.
  • A line between the line numbers and the code. The editor's gutter ends in a thin gray line down its full height, as in IntelliJ, so the numbers no longer run into the text.
  • Darker still. Every surface is a step darker (the editor from #131417 to #0D0E10, the panels and bars from #1B1C20 to #141518, the borders from #2B2D32 to #222428), the text a little dimmer and the editor's colours less bright; every word still reaches 4.5:1.
  • Full screen fills the screen on a Mac. The window drew its own frame, and macOS moves such a window into a full screen Space without making it bigger, so it sat at its old size in black. On a Mac the window is now the system's, its title bar see-through under the header: the red, yellow and green buttons are at the header's left, the green one or View → Enter Full Screen (⌃⌘F) gives full screen at the screen's size, and the window resizes from any edge as any Mac window does. Windows and Linux keep the header's − □ × (F11 for full screen). The app also starts with --add-exports=java.desktop/com.apple.eawt=ALL-UNNAMED, without which Java 21 refused the request.
  • One bar at the top, the page's own. As in an IDE, the window's bar is the page's toolbar: the sandbox's main.kts, +, env, Run and export; the Models page's tabs; Settings' back arrow and its sections as tabs, which scroll to them. The row the window had over each page is gone, 31dp back on every page, and there is no title.
  • Fewer words. A template is one line in the Templates pane, its about line and tags in the name's tooltip, Load an icon; Running in the background shows only with a run in it. Settings rows are a name and a control, the rest in their tooltips. The Metrics charts have short titles (Per label, Confusion matrix, Training by epoch, Calibration…) and no legend in sentences, which the Guide tab has; the Try line says Ask it something; the sidebar's tips are the pages' names. The About tab's Reveal folder stands at the end of the Where line again, however long the path.
  • The console reads from the top down, as a terminal does. The >>> prompt is on the line after the output, not in a bar at the foot of the pane: a fresh console is the greeting and the prompt at the top, each line pushes the prompt down, and once the pane is full it scrolls with the prompt at its foot. A click under the prompt puts the cursor in it. The prompt has no hint in it, only a blinking block cursor (an outline while the console hasn't the keyboard); the hint is the tooltip of >>>, and the send arrow is gone: Enter sends.
  • The console greets you as Python does. Amie pilot 1.0.0 (default, Nov 06 2026, 02:23:55) [Kotlin 2.1.0, JDK 21.0.11] on darwin, then Type "help", "sessions", "terminate all" or log("hi") for more information.; the input line's prompt is >>>. Clear and a run leave it there.
  • Run details, off by default. The console strip shows only its level toggles, Find, Details and Clear: no Finished in 0s, no memory line under it. Settings → Editor → Console → Run details brings them back, over the editor too while the console is hidden.
  • + beside main.kts. A new template in one click: the editor is emptied (the script in it kept under Previous scripts), the Templates window opens on the save form with the cursor in Name.
  • A double click on Load no longer loads twice. The second click could land on another row, often a Previous script, which put back the script just replaced, so a loaded template seemed to jump back. A Load within a second of another is ignored.
  • The console shows only what the script logs. Running pluginDir/main.kts, Finished in 0s and the Resources: line are at the internal level now, off at start: the strip over the console already says how the run went and what it used. A script that logs nothing leaves the console closed. A session the script left open is still named, at info.
  • log takes any value. log(pkg.run("scan")) was a type mismatch, since a package answers a list; log, info, error, data and output now take any value, a list or an array one element a line, a map key: value.
  • New template. The Templates window has a New template button at the top: it starts a new, empty script (the one in the editor is kept under Previous scripts) and opens the save form with the cursor in Name. It used to keep the script in the editor, which made copies of whatever was open.
  • Talk to Amie exports. Its Whisper and voice were taken for intent models and stopped the export; they now go along with speech.jar, and a script that opens only speech or text models carries no encoder.
  • Export from a script. exportJvm("main.kts") writes the same bundle as Export…; planOnly = true only says what would go in. See Scripting API.
  • ortAsync and handleBy. ortAsync("warm") { } is ortClosable on a thread of its own, returning a job that ends with the script; handleBy({ e -> "" }) { } gives the handler's value when the block throws, never for a stop or a cancel. See Scripting API. A running block is a row of the Sessions tab, Background block, with Terminate.
  • The export panel after writing. Show it stands alone: the export button, which had nothing left to write into that folder, no longer squeezes in beside it.

  • Words level with their icons, badges that fit their words. Text that named no line height took Material's 24sp, and Compose Desktop put that line's room nearly all above an 11-13sp word, so words sat low: under the icon of a button or a list row, at the bottom of a badge. Such text now has its font's own line. A list row's icon sits on its name's line, the flags and the meta under the name. The UI goldens are now taken in the app's theme, as the window shows it; before, they never had the 24sp line, so they never saw this.

  • Builds embed about five times quicker. The encoder takes the rows 32 at a time, each batch rows of the same number of tokens, so 1,000 rows take about 2.1 s instead of 11 on a Mac and the benchmark ends in 17 s instead of 26. The vectors are the same to the bit as one row at a time, so a model trains exactly as before; rows of different lengths are never mixed, because padding them moved the vectors by a few millionths.

  • The encoder stops copying what nobody reads. Every answer used to copy its whole hidden state into a list that nothing read.
  • setup.sh is in AMP/setup/. It sets up the whole AMP folder, not only the voice, so it moved out of voice/: run ./AMP/setup/setup.sh from the repository.
  • Talk to Amie says where a turn's time went. Took … ms: hearing …, intent …, Llama …, voice …, playing … in the console after each turn, so a slow answer shows which part was slow. See What happens to what you say.

docs.title: The app says what it waits for
docs.text:
• Nothing loads blank any more. A list that is still reading says "Reading the models…" with three soft dots instead of "No models yet"; a button whose work runs keeps its word, "Opening…", with the dots alive after it; the console's last line shows them while a text model loads or the builder embeds and fits; the thin line under the console and the build line of the Models list are the same line. Nothing shows for the first 150 ms, so a quick read never flickers. One component draws all of it, Loading.kt, listed in the components.
  • Every model is under AMP/models/. bert/ as before, intents/ for the trained intent models (was modules/), text/ for Llama and Qwen (was textModels/), speech/ for Whisper and the voices (was pluginDir/config/speech/models/). The app moves an older install there when it starts, one rename a folder, nothing copied, nothing deleted; with both an old and a new folder there it reads the new one and says in the console which to tidy. speech.properties is pointed at the new folder. See The AMP folder.

docs.title: Darker, and a console like an IDE's
docs.text:
• Easier on the eyes. Every surface is darker (the editor went from #1E1F22 to #131417, the panels from #2B2D30 to #1B1C20), no words are pure white any more, and the accents are calmer. Sign-in's white button is the app's blue, and right-click menus are dark on every page.
  • The console works like an IDE's terminal. ⌘F finds in the output, ⌘K clears, the arrow keys bring back what you typed, a copy over several lines keeps them apart, a main.kts:12 or a web address anywhere on a line is a link, and ANSI colours are drawn. See the output console.

docs.title: Talk to Amie, on models the app manages
docs.text:
• Models answer in the background. val job = model.inBackground("text") returns at once, and job.await(), job.done and job.cancel() follow it. Only so many run at once, the rest wait their turn on the Sessions tab, and when memory runs short the app closes idle ortTimed and ortLimited sessions first.
  • Text models run inside the app. ONNX Runtime GenAI exports in AMP/models/text/<name> open with initMod("name"), on the app's own ONNX Runtime (1.31.1 now). They are in Still open, count in a run's memory, end with Terminate and with the ortClosable around them.
  • Stop stops. A call of a package runs on a thread of its own, so Stop ends a script at once even when the package reads a device for seconds, and a loop can't go round again after it.
  • Scripts can wait to be called. input() in main.kts now reads what is typed in the console, and standard input in an exported bundle, so a script with a main() loads nothing until you ask. eof ends its input and Stop ends the wait. Exports now carry text models.
  • Amie is less dumb. It listens until you stop talking, understands many more ways of asking, and when unsure lets Llama read your words, so it picks out sites, files and days, and says when it didn't catch you instead of guessing. Web questions are answered from Wikipedia and the news, and files.jar opens, creates, reads and finds files.
  • The window keeps up. It is no longer see-through, which it never needed, so the Mac has less to do for each frame. The face draws on its own thread, and only copies its finished picture to the window. If the window's thread still stalls, the log says where.
  • Stopping a model can't take the app down. Closing a session or pressing Stop while a model is running used to free memory the run was still using, which crashed the whole app. A stopped run now ends first, and its session closes after it.
  • Amie answers sooner. Supertonic 3 is the voice now: it speaks about five times faster than Kokoro did, so a one-sentence reply starts in about 0.6 s instead of 2 s. Its model is under OpenRAIL-M. speaker= picks one of ten voices and steps= trades speed for quality; Kokoro and Piper still work with use.
  • Amie plays music. spotify.jar plays, pauses, skips and says what is on in the Spotify app, so "play Daft Punk" and "what song is this" work by voice. Without keys a name opens as a search in Spotify; with a clientId and clientSecret of your own in its settings, it plays straight away.
  • Amie does more by voice. Say "turn it up", "dark mode", "take a screenshot", "how much space is left", "close this tab" or "what are my newest files". It tells you how many emails are unread, and the face falls asleep when you stay quiet.
  • The jars do more. Mail counts, shows and marks read. The browser reads news and lists or closes tabs. Mac sets dark mode, takes screenshots and reads disk space. Files appends, renames and moves. Memory lists what's recent. The face is happy, sad, surprised or asleep.
  • Speech models are models. initMod("whisper") and initMod("voice") open them by name. They show on the Sessions tab under that name, and blocks and Terminate handle them like any other model. This needs the new speech.jar.
  • Ask a model what it can do. model.can("chat"), can("classify"), can("fineTune"), can("hear") or can("speak") tell you before you call it.
  • The app lands in half the time. The sandbox draws in about a second and freezes for much less on the way, on a start after the first. The editor's line numbers exist only near what's on screen, the app goes straight to the sandbox, and ./gradlew run keeps a class archive in build/. Packaged apps don't get the archive yet.
  • Amie has a face. face.jar shows an animated face over your windows that smiles, listens, thinks, loads and talks. A script sets the mood with face.run("think").
  • Closing keeps it running. Close the window while a script runs and it goes on in the background. The face in the menu bar opens the window again or quits.
  • Amie is a companion. It greets you, remembers what you tell it, reads your email, drafts replies and sends them only after you say yes, opens the browser and apps, and handles volume, the calendar and reminders, through four new jars with no keys.
  • The console runs script. Type log("hi") with nothing running and it runs in the background. It keeps going while you work or close the sandbox, and terminate console ends it.
  • The console reads like a Run window. While a script waits at input(), what you type is its input, shown in green, and the hint says so. Every red line now starts with the exception's name, or with Error.
  • The editor follows the caret. The arrow keys and typing move the page, so the caret never leaves the view.
  • The console has colours. Who wrote a line, strings, paths, numbers, session ids, and words like done, failed and warning each stand out. The words themselves stay as they were.
  • patchBy handles a failed command. shell("x").patchBy { error -> ... } sends what a failed command said to anything: a model, a voice, the console.
  • Talk to Amie runs without Python. speech.jar hears with Whisper and speaks with Kokoro, a natural voice with 11 speakers, set up in the Packages tab. It can now also open a terminal, close all of them, edit a file, open one in vim and run brew install, and it says out loud why a command failed.
  • Talk to Amie starts when you type talk in the console. It hears you, picks what to do with a BERT intent model, then gets the weather, lists or finds files, looks something up, or answers. See voice.md.

docs.title: The sandbox looks and works like an IDE
docs.text:
The app now uses the fonts and dark colours of the JetBrains IDEs: JetBrains Mono for code, Inter for everything else. The editor paints Kotlin as the IDE does, with functions, properties, named arguments, and what ${} holds in a string each in their own colour. The script API is in italics.

The templates and the console are tool windows that stand side by side, opened from an icon rail or with ⌘1 and ⌘4. Nothing closes one to show the other. Drag a window's header to the left, right or bottom edge to move it, and the line at its edge to size it; both are kept. The console's Recent runs and Still open are tabs, and it ends in a one-line prompt. See The sandbox.

Long titles are cut with an ellipsis and read whole in their tooltip, so they no longer push other labels away. A narrow model header puts its buttons on their own line, and tabs that don't fit go to a second line.

docs.title: Templates end with the block that called them
docs.text:
A template called in an ortClosable block now ends when that block ends, and what it opened closes with it. Before, it went on running after the block, and its session stayed open. This holds at any depth, so a template called by a template ends too, and a delegate used again in a later block starts a new run.

ortClosable("one question") {
    val label by template("Function: label a text")
    log(label("turn the lights on"))
}
// The template has ended here, and its model session is closed

docs.title: Function templates
docs.text:
A new Functions group of starters are templates you call like functions. Each takes a line of input and answers with a line: Function: clean a text, Function: count words, Function: label a text and Function: label and score. Four more show how to combine them: Function: clean, then label, Functions: a pipeline in ortClosable, Functions: keep the model between calls and Functions: a command as a function. An existing AMP folder gets them once. See Scope functions.

What landed in the update of 31 October 2026, and where to read more about each part.

docs.title: Scope functions
docs.text:
ortClosable, ortStatic, ortTimed and ortLimited take a block and decide how long what it opens stays open.

// Closed when the block ends, however it ends: a one-time use
val label = ortClosable("one time") {
    initMod("dummy").predict("turn the lights on")
}

// Stays open across runs, under a name you can free
val search = ortStatic("search") { initMod("dummy") }
log(search.predict("what's the weather"))

// Stays while it is used: freed by itself once nothing has asked it for 40 seconds
val recent = ortTimed("recent", 40) { initMod("dummy") }

// At most three package instances under the name, the oldest closed when a fourth is opened
val pool = ortLimited("pool", 3) { initMod("echo-1.0.jar") }

ortScopes.print().forEach { log(it) }     // what each scope holds
ortScopes.free("search")                  // closes what search holds
  • ortTimed(name, idleSeconds) { } keeps what its block opens like ortStatic, and frees it once nothing has used it for that long: the block not run again, no session it holds asked. One daemon timer serves every timed scope, and the Sessions tab counts down on its rows, as in timed recent, 40s left.
  • ortLimited(name, max) { } keeps at most max sessions under the name, freeing the oldest first when one more is opened; the tab says limited pool, 2 of 3.
  • ortForever is ortStatic now. A saved script that calls it still runs, the console says the new name, and the editor no longer offers it.

The Models page, Sessions tab, says which scope holds a session, as in static search. The whole starter is Scope functions: ortClosable and ortStatic in the sandbox's Templates pane; an existing AMP folder gets it once, and one that has it under its old title gets it renamed and brought up to date, as long as it is still the starter.
