See Scope functions.

docs.title: sessionMod
docs.text:
sessionMod("name") is a model to ask and nothing more: a snapshot of the head it has now. It can't train or change the model, leaves no trace in its log, and stays on its head when the model is trained again. It was called sharedModel until now; a saved script that says so still runs, and the console says the new name.

val m = sessionMod("dummy")                  // an object
log(m.predict("turn the lights on"))

val same by sessionMod("dummy")              // the same thing, as a delegate

val label = sessionMod("dummy") {            // for one block, gone when the block ends
    predict("turn the lights on")
}

See Ask without touching the model.

docs.title: Background templates
docs.text:
coroutineTemplate starts a saved template in the background while the script goes on. main.kts feeds it lines, the template reads them with input() and answers with output(text).

val job = coroutineTemplate("Background template: a reader")   // starts the saved template and goes on
job.send("turn the lights on")           // a line for its input()
log(job.receive())                       // its next output()
job.closeInput()                         // no more input is coming
log(job.await())                         // waits for the end

Each background run shows on the Sessions tab, keeps running after the run that started it, and says what it used when it ends. The two halves are starters in the Templates pane: Background templates: coroutineTemplate, which you load and Run, and Background template: a reader, the template it starts; an existing AMP folder gets them once. See Scripting API.

docs.title: Run several saved templates at once
docs.text: Run in background, the play icon on each row of the Templates pane, starts a saved template beside the script in the editor. The pane counts what runs, and each run has its live figures and Stop. Before a start, memory is checked: too little and it is refused, saying what is short and what to close. See Templates in the background.

docs.title: Delegate to a template
docs.text:
template("name") calls a saved template like a function, on one run:

val reader by template("reader")
log(reader("turn the lights on"))         // starts it, sends the line, returns its next output()
log(reader("what is the weather"))        // the same run
reader.close()                            // closes its input and waits

A failed template makes the call throw. When the script ends its template values are closed for it. Stop on a script, and cancel() or Terminate on a run, now end what it started, nested runs included; a template can't start itself. See Scripting API.

docs.title: Shell commands
docs.text:
shell and shellScript run commands and script files on this computer, in your login shell.

val r = shell("du -sh ~/Documents")
log(r.out)
shellScript("~/bin/backup.sh", listOf("--dry-run"))

The output follows in the console as it arrives. A command that fails turns the console's error level on, so its reason is in view. A command stops at its timeout, 120 seconds unless you give another, and when the app exits. Only a script in the sandbox can run one: the HTTP endpoints have no way to. See Scripting API.

docs.title: Exporting a script, compiled
docs.text: The export square on the strip over the editor (⌘E) makes a folder that runs the script with plain java, and by default the script and its templates go in compiled to classes: no compiler in the bundle, no compile at start, Java 21 or newer. The pane lists every saved template to take along; java -jar run.jar --template "name" runs one, --list says what there is, and templates called with template("name") or coroutineTemplate go along and call each other in the bundle as they do here. A script that calls two templates comes to 20 MB, starts and ends in 0.3 s and peaks at 87 MB, where the old way took 189 MB, 4.3 s and 430 MB. The pane ends on the bundle's path, its size and the exact java -jar line, with Copy. Script keeps the old way, the text with the compiler beside it. A script that doesn't compile is refused with its errors and nothing is written. See Exporting a script.

docs.title: Resources for every run
docs.text:
Each run ends with what it used: memory and its peak, heap, CPU time and ONNX Runtime calls, then the sessions left open. Recent runs shows a short form of the same line, and background templates print it too. A background template's line doesn't count its own run, or the runs that hold it, among the sessions left open.

Resources: memory 1.20 GB, peak 1.40 GB, 180.0 MB more than before · heap 340.0 MB of 4.00 GB · cpu 2.10 s · ort 12 runs in 640 ms · sessions 3 opened, 2 closed, 1 still open
Still open: web-ample #3 (static search)

See The sandbox.

The Models page, Sessions tab, has a Scripts section too: each script and template that ran, what it holds, its answers, its CPU and what it allocated; while main.kts runs, what its meter reads so far is under it.

Every session's row has a resources line under it, in file sizes, since ONNX Runtime doesn't say what it holds: a model session its head and its encoder (head 9 KB · encoder 415.6 MB, shared by 3 · 12 ms a run · last used 3s ago; the encoder is named once with how many share it), a package its jar, a bare ONNX session its file, a group the sum of its heads, and a background template what its meter reads right now (memory 1.20 GB, peak 1.40 GB · heap 340.0 MB of 4.00 GB · cpu 2.10 s · ort 12 runs in 640 ms). Over the rows, a totals line: what the process holds, how much of that is the encoders, the heap against its limit, and how many sessions are open and what they weigh together (Process 1.85 GB, of which encoders 415.6 MB · heap 340.0 MB of 4.00 GB · 20 sessions weigh 436.0 MB). See Running sessions.

docs.title: Autocomplete for block functions
docs.text: The editor offers every block function with its braces, as a script writes it, with the caret inside: ortClosable { }, sessionMod("") { }. After m. on a model, and inside a sessionMod block, it offers that model's own functions.

docs.title: Modules that miss something are refused
docs.text: initMod no longer opens a model or package that lacks something. It stops before anything opens and names what is missing: an encoder file, a head, labels that don't match, or a package config still holding its template. The same check backs the requirements list on the Models page. See Running sessions.

docs.title: The app
docs.text:
• Memory is watched while templates run, not only when they start: a light watch (a thread that exists only while a template goes in the background, one look a second) stops the newest template when the free heap stays under 32 MB for three looks and a collection doesn't bring it back, one at a time and newest first, with a plain console line saying which and why. main.kts is never stopped for it; it gets a warning line. See Background templates.
  • main.kts's Resources line no longer lists its own delegates as still open: the templates it called with template(...) are being closed at the moment the line is written, so it waits a moment for them and leaves them out; one started with coroutineTemplate goes on by design and is still listed (a background template's own line got the same fix earlier). See Resources.
  • A running script survives leaving the sandbox page: going to Models or Settings used to end main.kts with Stopped after. The run now belongs to the app, held apart from the page as the console's width and panes are, so it goes on while you look at Packages and Sessions, its lines keep reaching the console, and coming back shows it still running with its live status and a working Stop. See Running.
  • What runs, in the strip at the foot of the window: while main.kts or a template in the background goes, the strip's left end says how many (2 running). A click opens a small panel over it with a line for each: the name, its own figures (holds 416.5 MB · allocated 878.3 MB · cpu 1.39 s) and how long it has gone, and its own Stop. The cpu and the allocation are those of the thread its script runs on, and what it holds is the weight of the sessions it opened, an encoder shared with another run counted once, so a busy template and an idle one read differently. The Templates pane's rows show the same. With nothing running the strip is the one calm line it was, and its ✕ works as before. The figures are read off the UI thread. See Running in the background.
  • Cloud save: in the sandbox's Templates pane, under the save form, a logged-out person sees Saved here only and a quiet Log in to save to the cloud, which opens the log in page and comes back to the pane. Logged in, what you save (your templates, settings.json and main.kts, nothing else) is also kept in your account, a moment later from the background, and the pane says Saved here and to the cloud, or Saved here. Not saved to the cloud: with why. A failed send never touches the local save and is tried again on the next save and at the next login. At login, what the account has and this Mac doesn't comes down; where both changed, the newer stays in place and the other is kept under AMP/pluginDir/backup. Local saving works as before, logged in or not, and with the server down. See Cloud save.
  • Performance tests: org.example.project.perf measures start-up, the Models page over 60 models, what sessions, shared models and background runs hold and give back, every page and the command palette opened and closed over and over, the console under 40000 printed lines (it keeps between 18000 and 20000 of the newest, the file keeps all and is rotated at 20 MB), the console's commands including terminate all, and the figures on a run's Resources line, each against a budget. See Troubleshooting.
  • Console at its 20000-line cap drops its oldest 2000 lines at once, not one per new line: a script printing at the cap no longer makes the window compose every line again for each batch (1.2 s a batch of 100 lines became 0.2 s on average).
  • Appearance follows VS Code's Dark Modern: near-black panels with a slightly lighter sidebar and header, thin gray borders in place of filled blocks, one blue for the primary action, and red only on what ends or removes something. Buttons have 4px corners and two heights; the sidebar's items carry their names.
  • Layout polish: Settings is built like VS Code's, a title over a card of rows with the controls at the right, from the same buttons and toggles as the other pages. Every confirmation (destroy a model, delete a template or a file, restore a backup) and the error dialog share one box: 480 dp wide, a title, one muted line, and two 28 dp buttons at the right, the one that changes nothing first and the red one last. A template's name is cut with an ellipsis and its tags show only when they fit whole, so Load is never over them; the export of a template keeps its title in place while the page scrolls, and a package's flags are faint outlines with the same corners as the rest.
  • Status strip: the memory figure moved from the Models page to one strip across the foot of the window, on every page. Its ✕ hides it until the app closes, and Memory in the sidebar brings it back.
  • UI scale stops at 150%. A saved scale above that is brought down to it. See Settings.
  • Text starts with a capital and goes on in normal case everywhere. No label is in all capitals, apart from real acronyms such as ONNX and HTTP.
  • Stop: while a script runs the play square is a red stop square. Pressing it, or ⌘., interrupts the script, and the strip and Recent runs say Stopped after, neither finished nor failed. What the script opened stays open.
  • Left arrow closes the Templates panel as well as the console, and a second click brings them back as they were.
  • The status strip says nothing before a first run. The hint under the empty console is gone too.
  • Package repository: the search moved from Settings to the Models page, as the Repository section under the installed packages on the Packages tab. Settings keeps the account, the settings and the files. See Models page.
  • Live resources: while a script runs a line under the console strip reads memory 1.20 GB, peak 1.40 GB · heap 340.0 MB of 4.00 GB · cpu 2.10 s · ort 12 runs, read every second, so a script that grows is seen before it ends; the last run's figures stay there until the next run.
  • Still open: a fold under Recent runs lists every open session with Terminate, Free on one a kept scope holds, and Free all; the console's Still open: line opens it. The Sessions tab has Free on those rows too.
  • Console commands: free search, free all, terminate #3, terminate all, sessions, scopes, help and clear typed into the console's input run without a script. See The sandbox.
  • Console tooltips: every control on the console strip says what it is for, which way it is now and what a click does; the level toggles say how many lines they hide.
  • Editor crash: a long script at a high UI scale no longer crashes the editor pane.
  • Editor highlighting: a // or a # inside a string, an apostrophe, an escaped quote or a raw string no longer shifts the colours of everything after it onto the wrong characters; the editor reads strings and comments itself. A console place in a script with CRLF line endings lands before the \r.
  • Editor margins: a script longer or wider than its view no longer loses its margins when the editor takes the keyboard; the first letter of every line was cut off under the gutter and line 1 was half under the top edge.
  • Line numbers stand on the baseline of their lines. They sat a little above the text, and below it on line 1.
  • ONNX threads sleep when their session is idle instead of spinning, so an encoder, heads and a group open together don't take the cores of a Raspberry Pi between requests. -Damie.ort.threads=N sets how many threads a session gets. See Troubleshooting.
  • Builds on a small heap: the rows are embedded one at a time and only each row's sentence vector is kept, so ten thousand rows take 30 MB of heap instead of 2 GB.
  • The Models page opens on its models, not on their plots: the plots are drawn on a thread of their own and shown as they are ready, where the first read drew every model's before showing anything; a serving model's plots are drawn again at most every ten seconds instead of after every answer.
  • The Models page on a slow disk waits three times as long as its last read took before reading again, decodes a model's metrics history once per version of its file, and reads the process's memory from /proc on Linux and from one ps a second at most elsewhere.
  • Background templates run eight at a time on a heap of 512 MB or more and fewer on a smaller one, one per 64 MB.
  • Memory: the heap may grow to 35% of the machine's RAM; AMIE_JVM_ARGS adds JVM flags for one machine. An encoder that would not load, and an out of memory error nobody caught, each leave a console line saying what to do.
  • Startup timing: -Damie.timing=true prints when the window was composed and when the Models page had its first read.
  • Raspberry Pi 5 benchmark: --bench runs the app with no window and prints what each part costs on this machine (./scripts/pi-bench.sh on a Pi). Three things it found are fixed: the encoder's load no longer waits 4 seconds on DJL's call home (4.9 s to 0.8 s on a Mac, and nothing is sent to DJL's telemetry bucket any more), ONNX Runtime's library is unpacked once into AMP/cache/ort/ instead of at every start, and the script engine is warmed in the background so the first Run answers in a moment. See Raspberry Pi 5.

docs.title: Packages
docs.text:
google-sheets.jar and google-docs.jar join the other Google packages in jar-jar, on the shared Google code from amie-packages. janitor-ai.jar asks any OpenAI-compatible chat API over plain REST.

Package Commands google-sheets.jar tabs, read, write, append, create google-docs.jar read, create, append, replace janitor-ai.jar ask (the default: a prompt, or a chat completions request as JSON), raw, models

Both Google packages need google.properties filled in, so initMod refuses them until it is. To set them up, enable the Sheets and Docs APIs in your Google project, copy the jars to AMP/pluginDir, and authorize unless an authorize --all token already covers them:

java -jar google-sheets.jar authorize "<pluginDir>/config/google-sheets"

janitor-ai.jar speaks the OpenAI chat completions format (POST /chat/completions, GET /models) with the JDK's HTTP client and nothing else: no SDK, no dependency. Copy it to AMP/pluginDir; the first initMod("janitor-ai.jar") writes AMP/pluginDir/config/janitor-ai/janitor-ai.properties and refuses the jar until the file is filled in. Paste the URL and the key there: url= takes the base URL ending in /v1, or the full .../chat/completions address, the same thing JanitorAI's API settings take; key= the API key (sent as Authorization: Bearer, kept on this machine, never logged); model= the model name (models lists what the server offers); system= an optional system prompt. It works with any OpenAI-compatible server, a local one included: http://localhost:11434/v1 for Ollama or http://localhost:1234/v1 for LM Studio, with key= left empty. run(prompt) answers the assistant's text only, so answer(prompt) is the reply; an error names the HTTP status and what to do (401: the key, 404: the URL, 429: wait).

val ai = initMod("janitor-ai.jar")
log(ai.answer("say hi in three words"))
ai.close()

docs.title: Sandbox layout
docs.text: The rule beside the editor now moves in a small window or at a large UI scale, and stays under the pointer after it overshoots. The console and templates stay as you left them when you come back from the Models or Settings page. See the sandbox.
